Every oyzu command, the options all commands share, output modes and exit status.
oyzu auth signs you in to an Oyzu platform account by approving a code in a browser, reports the local session and signs out.
oyzu build compiles, tests and packages every target with its native tools, previews the plan, checks rules and writes a dist/ bundle you can verify.
oyzu cache shows where the local action cache lives and how large it is, explains why a stage's cache key changed, and clears cached results.
oyzu config shows, explains, validates and edits the oyzu.toml configuration cascade, lists profiles and prints JSON Schemas for build.yaml and oyzu.toml.
oyzu discover shows the targets Oyzu found, which builder handles each and why, and can declare them in build.yaml or check that build.yaml is complete.
oyzu exec runs a command with the project's locked tools on PATH, oyzu which prints the tool path the project would use, and oyzu env shows or exports the environment.
documents.s: oyzu exec, oyzu which and oyzu env

documents.t: oyzu inspect checks that a build bundle's files match their recorded digests and can verify release provenance; oyzu history lists and summarizes retained builds.
oyzu pin, install, update, uninstall and reshim declare, lock, install and remove a project's tools.
documents.s: oyzu pin, install, update, uninstall and reshim

documents.t: oyzu lock writes and checks debs.lock.yaml and apks.lock.yaml, reviewable records of every Debian or Alpine package a Docker image installs.
Find builder plugins, see which one each target of your project uses and why, list installed releases, and update the plugin selections locked in oyzu.lock.
oyzu publish uploads a finished build's artifacts to OCI registries or GitHub releases without an account, or requests governed publication from a platform.
oyzu release check asks a platform whether a built dist/ would ship in each environment, and oyzu secrets manages an account's write-only secrets.
oyzu run lists the tasks Oyzu found in your project and runs one with the project's pinned tools, passing extra arguments through.
oyzu scan runs the scanners your configuration or policy selects, such as Gitleaks, Trivy, Grype and SonarQube, against the inputs a build recorded.
oyzu activate, deactivate, shell install and shell remove put a project's pinned tools on PATH as you change directories, and oyzu trust allows a project's environment settings.
documents.s: oyzu activate, deactivate, shell and trust

documents.t: oyzu tools inspects tool records without running any tool - what is in effect, what is installed, available versions, the signed tool index, catalog requests and lock checks.
A map of Oyzu's parts, from the files in your repository to the bundle a build leaves behind, with links to each concept.

Run oyzu install --frozen, oyzu run list, oyzu build --plan, oyzu build --isolated --full and oyzu inspect dist. Native go.work owns both modules. Run oyzu install --frozen, oyzu build --plan, oyzu build --isolated --full and oyzu inspect dist. Native discovery chooses node/package; no build.yaml is needed. Create a separate consumer directory, run the selected npm with npm install --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --offline /absolute/path/to/the/delivered.tgz, then call require("oyzu-example-greeting").hello("developer"). Expect Hello, developer, from the delivered package. The consumer must use the collected archive, without source links or a registry publication.

Run oyzu install --frozen, oyzu build --plan and oyzu build --full for the native Rust host lane. Run its delivered executable with developer; expect Hello, developer! Built with Oyzu. Then provision the documented Rust cross-platform executor, locked target toolchains and Docker before running oyzu build --all-platforms --full. oyzu is one executable with a command for each job: build, run tasks, manage tools, inspect configuration and check results. This section has a page per command with its options, example output, --json shape and common errors. oyzu --help, oyzu <command> --help and oyzu help <command> work offline, outside any project and without an account. Help never loads configuration or contacts a service (CLI help). Example output in this section comes from a Windows machine. Paths are shortened with …, and versions, digests, times and IDs on your machine will differ.
The groups match oyzu --help.

Command What it does Page oyzu run [TASK] List tasks, or run one development task run oyzu build [TARGETS] Build native artifacts, run checks, preview the plan build oyzu publish Publish finished artifacts to configured destinations publish oyzu lock Write or check OS package locks for Docker targets lock oyzu cache status|clear|explain Inspect or clear the local action cache cache oyzu scan Run policy-selected scanners against a build's recorded inputs scan oyzu discover Show the targets Oyzu found and which builder handles each discover oyzu inspect [BUNDLE] Check a build's recorded files against their digests inspect and history

Command What it does Page oyzu pin Lock tool requirements without installing install family oyzu install [TOOLS] Install configured tools, or declare, lock and install named ones install family oyzu update [TOOLS] Move locked versions forward within each requirement install family oyzu uninstall TOOLS Remove tool declarations and their lock entries install family oyzu reshim Refresh installed-tool shims and activation launchers install family oyzu engine install Install a verified engine archive, or this oyzu with its Linux member for isolated builds, for your user engine staging oyzu exec -- COMMAND Run a command with the project's locked tools exec, which, env oyzu which COMMAND Print the path of the tool this project would use exec, which, env

Command What it does Page oyzu env Show the project environment, or print it as shell assignments exec, which, env oyzu config … Show, explain, validate and edit configuration; print JSON Schemas config oyzu trust [PATH] Allow a project's environment and PATH settings shell and trust oyzu shell install|remove Add or remove shell integration in a startup file shell and trust oyzu activate SHELL Print shell activation code shell and trust oyzu deactivate [SHELL] Print code that restores the shell session shell and trust

These commands talk to an Oyzu platform account. Everything else works without one. Command What it does Page oyzu auth login|status|logout Sign in, check the local session, sign out auth oyzu release check Ask whether the build in dist/ would ship release and secrets oyzu secrets list|create|set|rm Manage the account's write-only secrets release and secrets

Command What it does Page oyzu tools … Inspect tool records, versions, the tool index and trust tools oyzu plugins … Find plugins, see which one a target uses, update locked selections plugins oyzu history [ID] List retained build runs, or summarize one inspect and history

Every command accepts these, before or after the command name: oyzu --json build and oyzu build --json are the same. Anything after -- belongs to the child process and Oyzu never reads it. Option Effect -C, --directory <DIRECTORY> Run from this directory, as if you had cd'd there first --json Return machine-readable results and errors -v, --verbose... Show debug diagnostics; repeat (-vv) for trace -q, --quiet... Hide routine Oyzu progress, keeping results and child output --log-level <LOG_LEVEL> Set the diagnostic threshold: error, warn, info, debug or trace --root <ROOT> Use an explicit project root (also stops configuration inheritance from parent folders) --profile <PROFILE> Select a configuration profile --no-profile Disable profile selection --toolset <NAME> Use a toolset's tools ([toolsets.NAME.tools] in oyzu.toml) for exec, run, env, activate, which, install, update, uninstall and pin --local-overrides Include local configuration overrides --licenses Print this executable's embedded distribution notices and source identity -h, --help Print help -V, --version Print the version (top level only) oyzu -C services/api build --plan # plan a nested project without cd oyzu --root . discover # ignore oyzu.toml files in parent folders oyzu --toolset node24 exec -- node -v # use a toolset's Node instead of [tools] See configuration for profiles, toolsets and local overrides.

Human (default). Results lead with the outcome, then aligned tables and named sections. Color appears only on capable terminals and never carries meaning on its own. Redirected output and NO_COLOR=1 give plain text. Don't parse the human layout; use --json. JSON (--json). Standard output holds exactly one JSON result and nothing else. Oyzu's own diagnostics go to standard error as JSON Lines. Errors are an object with at least error and exitCode: $ oyzu --json build --bogus { "code": "CLI_USAGE", "error": "unexpected argument '--bogus' found\n\… to pass '--bogus' as a value, use '-- --bogus'", "exitCode": 2, "nextStep": "Run oyzu <command> --help for supported arguments." } Help and version text come back under output. Shell payloads (activate, deactivate, env --shell) print executable code by default and {"shell": …, "script": …} with --json. Result shapes can gain fields, so ignore fields you don't recognize. Quiet (-q). Hides routine progress and the live dashboard. Results, warnings, errors and native tool output stay. Verbose (-v, -vv, --log-level). Adds debug or trace diagnostics on standard error. It never changes what is built, cached or reported. When no flag is given, the OYZU_LOG environment variable accepts a level or target=level directives. More than two -v, more than one -q, or mixing these controls is a usage error. See diagnostic controls. oyzu build also has --output auto|plain|interactive to choose between linear output and the live dashboard. It changes presentation only.

A human error starts with ✗, the error code and the message, followed by what to do next. It also names the invocation ID, the oyzu version, the executable and the directory, so a pasted error explains itself: $ oyzu run nosuchCopy ✗ TASK_NOT_FOUND: no task "nosuch" in …\hello. Available tasks: build, format, format-check, install, lint, test. Run oyzu run to list tasks, or oyzu -C <project> run nosuch Next: Check the selected directory and name; use oyzu -C <project> to select a project. Invocation: 55840-1792551849171752700-1 … Output shortened. The other command pages show only the first lines of each error.

Scripts and CI can branch on the exit status without parsing text. Each command page lists its own cases. Status Meaning Typical codes 0 Success 1 The operation failed: a build or check failed, a tool was refused, or an error without a more specific class COMMAND_FAILED, TOOL_INSTALLATION_MISSING 2 The invocation was refused (bad arguments or conflicting flags), or a publication failed or was left unfinished CLI_USAGE, TOOL_FLAGS_CONFLICT, TOOL_SPEC_INVALID 3 Configuration or policy is invalid, or the build can't run on this machine CONFIG_*, POLICY_*, TOOL_NATIVE_MINIMUM_CONFLICT, NEEDS_DOCKER_DAEMON 4 A lock is missing or stale, or a slice's upstream result isn't cached TOOL_LOCK_STALE, TOOL_LOCK_MISSING, PLUGIN_LOCK_MISSING, UPSTREAM_NOT_CACHED 5 Something you named wasn't found (a task, a declared tool, a project), or a slice's handoff write failed TASK_NOT_FOUND, TOOL_NOT_DECLARED, TOOL_NO_PROJECT, HANDOFF_PUSH_FAILED 130 Interrupted with Ctrl+C. A build stops starting new work, ends its processes and keeps its logs oyzu run and oyzu exec return the child's own exit status. With --json, errors carry the same number in exitCode.
CLI help and CLI output: help catalog, presentation rules, JSON envelopes, redaction and diagnostic controls. Configuration: every setting and the oyzu.toml cascade. Capabilities and limitations.

Sign in to an Oyzu platform account, check your local session, or sign out. Only the platform commands (oyzu build --remote, oyzu run --remote, oyzu secrets and oyzu release check) use the session. Everything else Oyzu does stays local and needs no account. oyzu auth [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> Subcommand What it does login Sign in by approving a code in a browser, then store the session status Show the selected platform, account and local session state; contacts no server logout End this account's local session and ask the issuer to revoke it conformance Check this client's sign-in behavior against a built-in test issuer; needs no account None of the subcommands has its own options; the global options apply. Note: Experimental. Until your platform publishes the sign-in metadata Oyzu needs, login fails with AUTH_DISCOVERY_UNSUPPORTED.

Point Oyzu at the platform and account in your user configuration. A project file can't choose where your credentials go. oyzu config set --global platform.url https://platform.example.com oyzu config set --global platform.account payments Without this, login, status and logout stop right away with AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED and show the command to run.

oyzu auth login Oyzu uses the OAuth 2.0 device authorization flow (RFC 8628): It finds the platform's identity issuer from platform.url. It shows a web address and a short code. Approve the code in a browser on any device. It checks that you are an active member of platform.account. Only then does it store the session in your operating system's credential store: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or a Linux Secret Service provider. There is no plaintext fallback. A cancelled, denied or expired login stores nothing. login needs a terminal; without one it fails with AUTH_INTERACTION_REQUIRED before sending any request. The code is printed on standard error, so --json output stays parseable.

oyzu auth status --json oyzu auth logout status reads only local state and reports the platform, account and session state: absent, active, refreshing, reauthentication-required or logged-out. logout deletes this account's local session, then asks the issuer to revoke it and reports that result separately. If revocation couldn't be confirmed, it reports remote: refused, unreachable or not-advertised.
documents.s: oyzu auth status and oyzu auth logout

documents.t: Situation Credential OYZU_PLATFORM_TOKEN is set That token, as given At a terminal, no token set The stored session from oyzu auth login Unattended (CI, scripts, agents), no token and no provider selected None: AUTH_PROVIDER_REQUIRED. A stored session is never used without being asked for platform.authentication.provider (session or environment) chooses one explicitly. The credential is sent only to the origin of platform.url.

Runs this client's sign-in scenarios against a local test issuer with made-up credentials. It needs no account or network, prints one row per scenario, and exits 1 if any scenario fails. Use it to check the client itself, not your platform or credential store.

Exits 0 on success and 1 on any failure. Code Fix AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED Set platform.url and platform.account with oyzu config set --global. AUTH_INTERACTION_REQUIRED Run login from a terminal. In CI, set OYZU_PLATFORM_TOKEN instead. AUTH_PROVIDER_REQUIRED Unattended, with no token. Set OYZU_PLATFORM_TOKEN, or set platform.authentication.provider. AUTH_STORE_UNAVAILABLE Start or unlock your operating system's credential store. AUTH_NOT_A_MEMBER, AUTH_STEP_UP_REQUIRED You aren't an active member of platform.account, or the account needs stronger authentication. Nothing was stored. AUTH_DISCOVERY_UNSUPPORTED The platform doesn't publish the sign-in metadata yet. AUTH_REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED, AUTH_LOGIN_REQUIRED Run oyzu auth login again.
Platform sign-in and the credential provider.

Build every target, or the ones you name. oyzu build installs the pinned tools, runs each target's stages with its native commands (go build, npm run build, cargo build and so on), reuses results that haven't changed, and writes the outputs, a manifest, logs and reports to dist/. oyzu build [OPTIONS] [TARGETS]... Argument Meaning [TARGETS]... Target IDs; omitted means all targets. Required dependencies are included Target names are the ones oyzu discover prints.

You want to Run Build every target for this machine oyzu build Build one target (and what it depends on) oyzu build cli See what would run, without running anything oyzu build --plan Also run formatting, lint and tests oyzu build --full Report rule findings only oyzu build --check Build for another platform oyzu build --platform linux/arm64 Build every declared platform oyzu build --all-platforms See why a stage ran instead of being reused oyzu build --explain Build only what changed since a Git ref oyzu build --affected origin/main
The global options also apply.

Option Description --full Run all quality stages locally (also enabled by CI context) --context <CONTEXT> Pin the build context: local, pr, ci or release. Detected from CI provider variables by default; a pin can raise it, and can lower it only when no CI provider marker is present. Also OYZU_CONTEXT --platform <OS/ARCH> Build for this target platform instead of the host (repeatable): os/arch[/abi] such as linux/arm64 or windows/x86_64/msvc; amd64 and aarch64 are accepted. A target that doesn't declare it skips it --all-platforms Build every declared platform with the container executor; fails before running when any declared platform can't be built here --affected <AFFECTED> Build targets affected since a local Git ref, including dependents --optimized Build the optimized profile (cargo build --release) even when the artifacts stay local. Overrides build.optimized; policy still wins --no-optimized Build the development profile even when the artifacts are packaged, handed off, cached remotely or published. Overrides build.optimized --require-release Require authenticated exact-tag candidate or release coordinates. Missing evidence refuses the build before native actions run --release-profile <FILE> Independent exact hosted builder and source expectations for this run --verify-with <TOOLSET> Also run this toolset's verification run (repeatable): test the builds that use its tools with them ([toolsets.NAME] in oyzu.toml), in any context. What ships is still built with [tools] --verify-only <TOOLSET> Run only this toolset's verification runs (repeatable), not the selected builds' own stages. For a dedicated verification job, like the commands under .verify in oyzu build --plan --json --skip-verification Run no toolset verification runs here, for a workflow that runs each .verify entry of the plan in its own job. Each skipped run is named

Option Description --plan Preview stages and requirements without installing, downloading or running tools --stage <NAME> With --plan: show only this stage's analysis (for example build or test) --why <PATH> With --plan: explain whether a path is an input or output of each stage, and why --unknown With --plan: show only analysis facts that are unknown or over-approximate --facts With --plan: also list every raw analysis fact, grouped by kind --no-analysis With --plan: skip static analysis; every stage uses whole-target scope --check Run static analysis and the project's rule levels without preparing or running anything; exits non-zero on a blocking finding

Option Description --no-cache Run every action: don't reuse or store action results for this build --explain After the build, show why each stage was reused or ran: the first key component that changed since its last build --verify-contract Check each stage contract: run every confined action again with its whole target visible and compare the results. Reuses and stores nothing -j, --jobs <N> Run at most N preparation and build workers at once. Overrides build.jobs and OYZU_BUILD_JOBS; the default follows available CPUs

Option Description --offline Require cached tools and dependencies; download nothing --frozen Replay the plugin selections in oyzu.lock; fail rather than resolve or rewrite it --store <STORE> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store --isolated Use the container executor, which builds from a captured copy of the source --no-docker Never contact a Docker engine (also OYZU_NO_DOCKER=1). A selected target that needs one stops the build before anything runs, with exit status 3 --image <IMAGE> Run a manager's isolated work on your own execution image instead of the base image, e.g. npm=node:22-trixie-slim --execution-images-from <BUNDLE> Reuse the exact execution images from a retained build bundle. Source and engine, plugin and tool selections must match, and current controls apply --engine-development Keep this development executable instead of the pinned engine; requires local policy permission --connector-bindings <CONNECTOR_BINDINGS> Host-owned connector endpoints and authorization environment references

Option Description --remote Build the pushed HEAD on a platform pool and follow it here. The pool always runs full checks in isolation; Ctrl+C cancels the remote run. With --plan: preview what the pool would run, with each target's platform and executor needs, without contacting the platform --download <DIR> With --remote: download the run's outputs into this directory --slice Build only the named targets, in isolation. Every other target they need is reused from the caches and never built; a missing one stops the build with UPSTREAM_NOT_CACHED (exit status 4) --handoff <OCI_URL> With --slice: the OCI repository (oci://host/path) read first for upstream results and written with this slice's own. A failed write fails the build with HANDOFF_PUSH_FAILED (exit status 5) --slice-plan <TARGET_ID> With --slice: a target ID from the original preview. Repeat for every preview target, including targets folded into another slice

Option Description --output <OUTPUT> Presentation only: auto and plain use linear output, interactive opts into the live dashboard. Default auto Note: Local host builds are the everyday path. These options are experimental: --check and plan analysis (advisory), --remote (needs a platform account), --slice/--handoff, --verify-contract, --isolated and --require-release. See limitations.

A plain oyzu build on your machine is a fast build: it runs the build stage and only the checks set to required. --full, or a CI context, adds tests, lint and format checks. See check levels. Full and CI builds, and the tags and conventional version strategies, can fetch missing Git history from public GitHub HTTPS remotes to work out the version. Your checkout and HEAD don't change. Fast local builds and --plan never fetch. See version inference.

--plan only reads files. It installs, downloads and runs nothing, and doesn't touch dist/: $ oyzu build --planCopy Planning hello Windows x86_64 (host) · Local · context local · Fast build requested ​ Build preview Execution: host · No tools installed, dependencies downloaded or build actions run. ​ project · go/app · windows/x86_64 Executor: host Profile: development · local dist only (no difference: the Go compiler always optimizes) Stage Selection Details build selected Native commands and report bindings resolve during preparation format-check skipped fast local build lint skipped fast local build test skipped fast local build ​ Tool requirements · availability not checked Requirement Kind Constraint Targets Source oyzu:go minimum-version >=1.22 project go.mod go oyzu:go request 1.22 project go.mod (native pin) ​ Unresolved until preparation • Tool installations and executor prerequisites have not been checked. • Application dependency availability and native metadata require preparation. • Exact commands, additional native stages, artifacts and report bindings require preparation. … Output shortened. The last section lists what can only be known once the build prepares.

$ oyzu build --fullCopy Building hello windows/x86_64 (host) · local · context local · full ​ ── Prepare ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ✓ Configuration Loaded and validated <0.1s ✓ Tool versions Resolved and locked 10.9s … ✓ Tools 1 tool pinned · 0 installed now 0.4s go 1.22.12 already installed detected from go.mod ​ ── Facts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Branch master Version project 0.0.0-dev.g1e5ffa22c338 Context local (detected, no CI signal) … ​ ── Plan ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── format lint test build project run run run run ​ ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 00:26 ✓ project build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=fals… executed 13.7s 00:32 ✓ project test go test -json -coverprofile=C:\Us… executed 5.9s 00:33 ✓ project lint go vet ./... executed 1.2s 00:34 ✓ project format-check gofmt -l . executed 0.2s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── project dist/project/windows/x86_64/project-0.0.0-dev.g1e5ffa22c338.exe 2.0 MB development ​ Tests run now 1 passed · 0 failed · 0 skipped (1 collected reports) Coverage project: 50.0% (1/2 statements) ​ ✓ Build succeeded 1 target · 4 executed · 34.4s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 20376-1792551752991392800-1 Output shortened. The sections always come in this order: Prepare (configuration, tools, workspaces), Facts (source and version), Plan (which stage runs for each target), Build (one row per action with its real command), Outputs, then the result. Failures and warnings get their own sections. The build output layout describes every row.

$ oyzu build --explainCopy … 00:02 ↺ project build reused was 2.2s … ✓ Build succeeded 1 target · 1 reused · 2.6s ​ Why each stage ran or was reused project:build — Reused Recorded selection: project (selected) Reuse: a stored result matches this key (run 33496-1792551834158101500, 2026-10-21T03:03:56Z) A reused result is always labelled reused. For one target after the fact, use oyzu cache explain.
documents.s: See why a stage was reused

documents.t: $ oyzu build --checkCopy Checking hello Windows x86_64 (host) · Local · context local · Fast build requested ​ ✓ Check passed: no blocking findings Static analysis only: nothing was installed, downloaded or executed. … A blocking finding makes --check exit 1.

--plan --why PATH answers "if I change this file, what rebuilds?" using static analysis. In a Node package: $ oyzu build --plan --why src/greeting.mjsCopy … project:build · confidence: over-approximate · scope: predicted src/greeting.mjs → this stage reads or writes it (facts below) Path or name Confidence Source Why src/greeting.mjs exact build.mjs:3 file-read · copyFileSync ​ project:package · confidence: over-approximate · scope: predicted src/greeting.mjs → not an input or output of this stage …
documents.s: Ask which stages read a file

documents.t: When an action fails, the output gets a Failure section with the failing test or compiler message, the exit code, the log path and a command that re-runs only that target. The tutorial shows one. A failed build exits 1, and binaries from the previous successful build stay in place.

oyzu --json build prints the build-manifest record that is also written to dist/manifest.json: $ oyzu --json build { "actions": [ { "durationMs": 2229, "exitCode": 0, "id": "project:build", "status": "succeeded" } ], "artifacts": [ { "digest": "sha256:ed5cb4ccc3e5d67fb6a8080cf853e0ae7d2bcbd8cc915b06d383fcac4c8be3e3", "id": "project:primary", "path": "project/windows/x86_64/project-0.0.0-dev.g1e5ffa22c338.exe", "producer": "project:build", "size": 1985024 } ], "diagnostics": [], "envelopePath": "envelope.json", "evidence": [], "kind": "build-manifest", "planPath": "plan.json", "reports": [], "schemaVersion": "v1alpha1", "source": { "commit": null, "dirty": true, "treeDigest": "sha256:a98b850fd775…" }, "status": "succeeded", "targets": [ { "builder": "go/app", "id": "project", "path": ".", "platform": { "arch": "x86_64", "os": "windows" } } ] } oyzu --json build --plan prints a build-preview record instead: selection, targets[] (with executor, platform, needsDaemon and stages), tasks, requirements, analysis, matrix, verify, effects (all false, since nothing was downloaded, installed or run) and unresolved. CI pipelines use targets[], matrix and verify to fan out jobs. See read-only build preview.

Status When 0 The build, plan or check succeeded 1 An action failed, --check found a blocking finding, a target name is unknown, or preparation failed 2 Invalid arguments, or a handoff repository this client can't use 3 Invalid configuration (for example CONFIG_REFERENCE_UNKNOWN), or the build can't run here (NEEDS_DOCKER_DAEMON with --no-docker, NEEDS_USER_NAMESPACES) 4 A missing or stale lock, or UPSTREAM_NOT_CACHED in a --slice build 5 HANDOFF_PUSH_FAILED in a --slice build 130 Interrupted with Ctrl+C; logs and a failed bundle are kept

Message Cause and fix COMMAND_FAILED: unknown build target nosuch; available targets: project The name isn't a target. Run oyzu discover for the names. TOOL_LOCK_STALE oyzu.lock has no pin for a requirement (for example, go.mod changed). Run oyzu pin, then build again. CONFIG_REFERENCE_UNKNOWN oyzu.toml names a build, output or task that build.yaml doesn't declare. The message gives the file, line, column and the nearest valid name. NEEDS_DOCKER_DAEMON A target needs a container engine and --no-docker is set, or no engine is running. Start Docker or build that target elsewhere. TOOL_NATIVE_MINIMUM_CONFLICT A configured tool version is below what a native file requires (such as the go line in go.mod). Raise the configured version.

Local builds: selection, executors, platforms, preview and slices. Build tasks: stages, fast and full builds, optimized builds, task conditions. Build bundles: the dist/ layout and retention. Action cache and affected builds. Version inference, including authenticated release staging for --require-release. Remote runs for --remote.

Inspect or clear the local action cache. When nothing that affects a build stage has changed (toolchain, dependencies, stage definition, the source files it reads, the outputs it consumes), oyzu build reuses the stored result instead of running the stage again. The cache belongs to your user account and is shared by all your projects. oyzu cache [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> Subcommand What it does status Show where the local action cache lives, how large it is and how many entries it holds clear Remove every cached action result. Build bundles are never touched explain <TARGET> Show why a target's or stage's cache key last changed: the first key component that differs from the build before None of the subcommands has its own options; the global options apply. Note: The action cache is experimental. Results are reused only on the same machine and user account unless you set up a shared remote cache (action cache).

$ oyzu cache statusCopy Action cache ​ Location C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\cache\actions (default per-user location) Entries 552 results · 2841 blobs Size 9.9 GiB of 10.0 GiB retention budget Docker 5 images · 2.6 GiB of 20.0 GiB image budget (cache.dockerMaxMiB) Local use enabled … Platform Default location Linux $XDG_CACHE_HOME/oyzu/actions (or ~/.cache/oyzu/actions) Windows %LocalAppData%\Oyzu\cache\actions Set cache.dir in user or machine configuration to move it. At the end of a build, the least recently used results are removed when the cache is over its 10 GiB budget. oyzu --json cache status returns an action-cache-status record with location, locationSource, present, enabled, entries, blobs, bytes, budgetBytes and a docker object (images, bytes, budgetBytes).

oyzu cache explain [OPTIONS] <TARGET> Argument Meaning <TARGET> A target ID, or one stage's action ID such as api:build $ oyzu cache explain project:buildCopy Cache key explanation project:build ​ project:build (stage) Key d7dbf45c44f6 · since run 7340-1792534273646063700 · last seen run 7340-1792534273646063700 (2026-10-20T22:11:22Z) Result stored · the next build with these inputs reuses it Changed since run 13316-1792534220089452300: prepared dependencies changed (also: source files in scope; action definition: argv, env.OYZU_VERSION and 2 more; output of an earlier action: project:prepare) It reads recorded keys and runs nothing. Changed names the first part of the key that differs from the previous build of that stage, then the others. oyzu build --explain prints the same reasoning for every stage right after a build.

oyzu cache clear Removes every cached action result. Build bundles in dist/ hold their own copies and are never touched. clear needs the cache to itself: while a build is using it, clear fails and asks you to retry, so run it again after the build finishes. Don't delete store.lock by hand to get around this. To skip the cache for one build, use oyzu build --no-cache. To turn it off, set cache.local = false.
Status When 0 Success 1 An operation error, such as a cache that a running build is using 3 cache.dir set in a project file (CONFIG_SCOPE); set it only in user or machine configuration
Local action cache: what is reused, keys, controls, location, retention and the remote OCI cache. The action cache and the caching guide.

Inspect, explain and edit Oyzu's configuration. Settings come from a cascade: built-in defaults, machine and user configuration, every oyzu.toml from the repository root down to the target's folder, then oyzu.local.toml. oyzu config shows the merged result and where each value came from, and edits one file at a time. build.yaml (which builds exist) is a separate file; see discover. oyzu config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> Subcommand What it does show Show the resolved configuration get Read one resolved configuration value explain Explain where configuration values came from profiles List available configuration profiles validate Validate configuration and report diagnostics status Show configuration session status refresh Refresh the configuration session set Set a value in one chosen configuration file unset Remove a value from one chosen configuration file schema Print the JSON Schema of build.yaml or oyzu.toml, for editors Every subcommand accepts the global options. --profile NAME resolves (or, for set, writes into) that profile; --root and -C choose the project.

oyzu config show [OPTIONS] Option Description --global Read only the user configuration file, without merging other scopes --project Read only oyzu.toml in the selected directory --local Read only oyzu.local.toml in the selected directory $ oyzu config showCopy Configuration ​ Status: resolved Profile: none (base configuration) ​ Build Setting Value build.isolation auto build.jobs 4 ​ Cache Setting Value cache.dockerMaxMiB 20480 cache.local true cache.nativeMaxMiB 8192 … ​ Use oyzu config explain <key> for provenance; oyzu env for resolved environment values. Output shortened; the full view lists every group of settings. With --global, --project or --local, only that one file is read, without defaults. Values that look like credentials are hidden.

oyzu config get [OPTIONS] <KEY> Argument / option Description <KEY> The setting, such as build.jobs --global Read only the user configuration file, without merging other scopes --project Read only oyzu.toml in the selected directory --local Read only oyzu.local.toml in the selected directory oyzu config get build.jobs # 4 oyzu --json config get build.jobs # 4, as a bare JSON value With --json, the output is the bare JSON value, which is handy in scripts. A key with no effective value fails with CONFIG_INVALID_VALUE: setting has no effective value.

oyzu config explain [OPTIONS] [KEY] Argument / option Description [KEY] Limit the explanation to one setting --context <CONTEXT> Explain as this build context (local, pr, ci or release) applies its [context.<name>] values. Detected from the environment by default --target <TARGET> Resolve for this build target (a build.yaml target name): its folder chain decides which oyzu.toml files apply --global Read only the user configuration file, without merging other scopes --project Read only oyzu.toml in the selected directory --local Read only oyzu.local.toml in the selected directory After oyzu config set --project build.jobs 4: $ oyzu config explain build.jobsCopy Configuration explained Local · Profile: none (base configuration) Build context: local (detected, no CI signal) ​ Build Setting Effective value Last source build.jobs 4 …\hello\oyzu.toml ​ build.jobs Order Operation Source Scope Profile Context 1 default built-in — — — 2 replace …\hello\oyzu.toml project — — ​ Policy: no constraints on these settings. Output shortened. --context ci shows what a CI build would see; --target api shows what one target in a monorepo sees. --json adds byte positions, constraint sources, context signals and the configuration digest.

oyzu config profiles Lists the available profiles and which one is selected, and why. A profile is a named set of settings, selected with --profile, OYZU_PROFILE or a project default. CI selects the built-in ci profile automatically. Profiles never grant extra permissions and can't hold tools (use a toolset for that).

oyzu config validate [OPTIONS] Option Description --strict Fail on warnings too, listing each with its key, source and fix --all-profiles Validate every profile, not only the selected one $ oyzu config validateCopy Configuration ​ Diagnostics: (none) Valid: yes show and explain can succeed with Status: unresolved, so use validate as the configuration gate in automation. It exits non-zero on a validation failure. For builds that use an external builder plugin, validate checks the plugin's declared profile, required engine features and the general shape of with, using the installed package metadata. It never runs the plugin or refreshes the plugin catalog. The package must already be installed by a normal build; otherwise you get PLUGIN_NOT_ADOPTED or PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED with the next step. Plugin-specific option values are checked by the build itself.

oyzu config status oyzu config refresh status reports whether this machine is enrolled in managed configuration and the state of its policy cache, without going online. In standalone use it prints Enrolled: no and Mode: standalone. refresh fetches managed policy and reports its revision and offline deadline. It needs managed enrollment; standalone, there is nothing to refresh.

oyzu config set [OPTIONS] <--global|--project|--local> <KEY> <VALUE> oyzu config unset [OPTIONS] <--global|--project|--local> <KEY> Option Description --global Select the user (global) configuration file --project Select oyzu.toml in the selected directory --local Select oyzu.local.toml in the selected directory --json-value (set only) Parse VALUE as JSON, for arrays and objects Exactly one scope flag is required: $ oyzu config set --project build.jobs 4Copy Configuration ​ Destination: …\hello\oyzu.toml Updated: build.jobs Booleans and numbers are parsed by type; strings are taken literally. Edits keep unrelated comments and formatting, check known keys and types, and replace the file in one step. unset removes the value from that file so inherited values show through. Only an explicit --profile NAME writes into a profile. Tools aren't settings. Use oyzu install to declare them. Leaving out the scope flag is a usage error (CLI_USAGE, exit 2).

Prints the JSON Schema of build.yaml or oyzu.toml for editor completion and validation. It opens no project and needs no network. oyzu config schema [OPTIONS] [FILE] Argument Meaning [FILE] The file whose schema to print: build.yaml or oyzu.toml Without a file name, it lists both schemas and where each release publishes them: https://github.com/oyzuai/oyzu-releases/releases/latest/download/build.yaml.schema.json https://github.com/oyzuai/oyzu-releases/releases/latest/download/oyzu.toml.schema.json oyzu discover --write adds a # yaml-language-server: $schema=<URL> line to build.yaml; add it by hand to an existing file. For oyzu.toml, point Taplo or Even Better TOML at the URL. Offline, save the schema and point your editor at the file: oyzu config schema build.yaml > build.yaml.schema.json With a file name, the schema itself is printed, even in human mode, so you can redirect it. With --json, it is wrapped in a config-schema record under schema.

Status When 0 Success (show and explain succeed even when the status is unresolved) 1 refresh failed, or another operation error 2 Missing scope flag or other invalid arguments 3 Invalid configuration, a key with no value (CONFIG_INVALID_VALUE), a setting in the wrong scope (CONFIG_SCOPE), or a validation failure Common configuration codes: Code Fix CONFIG_SYNTAX The TOML is malformed. The message gives file:line:column; fix it in an editor. CONFIG_SCOPE A project file sets something it may not, such as cache.dir. Move it to user configuration. CONFIG_EDIT_CONFLICT Another process edited the file at the same time. Retry. CONFIG_PROFILE_TOOLS A profile contains tools. Use a toolset instead.
Cascading configuration: every setting, precedence, contexts, profiles, toolsets and policy. Editor schemas.

Show what Oyzu sees in a folder: each target (one buildable unit, such as a Go module, an npm package or a Cargo package), the builder that handles it, whether build.yaml or detection chose it, and where it lives. Discovery reads build.yaml and your native files. It never runs project code. oyzu discover [OPTIONS]

Option Description --write Declare every folder build.yaml leaves out, creating build.yaml if needed --check Write nothing; exit non-zero if a tracked folder holds a build that build.yaml neither declares nor lists under exclude: The global options also apply. When a build.yaml exists, only its builds are built. An entry can leave out uses when exactly one builder recognizes its folder. Folders that discovery recognizes but build.yaml leaves out are listed, never built. Inside Git, only tracked files count.

$ oyzu discoverCopy 1 target · 6 tasks discovered without running project code Project root: …\hello ​ project · go/app Chosen by detected from project files Location . Manager go Version 0.0.0 Part of builds build, format-check, lint, test Development tasks format, install ​ Target names are what `oyzu build <target>` accepts. … Part of builds are the stages oyzu build runs for this target. Development tasks are available only through oyzu run.

A single project works fine with no configuration. In a repository with several projects, declare them so a new folder never quietly becomes a build: $ oyzu discover --writeCopy Created build.yaml with 1 build Build Uses Folder project node/app . Only folders with Git-tracked files were considered. Review the change, then add `oyzu discover --check` to CI to catch new folders. The file it wrote: # yaml-language-server: $schema=https://github.com/oyzuai/oyzu-releases/releases/latest/download/build.yaml.schema.json builds: project: {uses: node/app, path: .}

$ oyzu discover --checkCopy Build inventory is current · 1 build declared Only folders with Git-tracked files were considered. When a folder isn't declared, it exits 1 and prints the line to add: $ oyzu discover --checkCopy error[INVENTORY_UNDECLARED]: there is no build.yaml; discovery finds 1 build here Folder Recognized by Line to add under builds: . go/app project: {path: .} Only folders with Git-tracked files were considered. fix: run `oyzu discover --write` to declare them, or list the folders that are deliberately not builds under exclude: in build.yaml

oyzu --json discover returns the full discovery record. Shortened to one target and one task: $ oyzu --json discover { "root": "…\\hello", "targets": { "project": { "builder": "go/app", "builder_selection": "inferred", "manager": "go", "name": "project", "path": "…\\hello", "version": "0.0.0" } }, "tasks": { "project:build": { "argv": ["go", "build", "./..."], "build_stage": true, "name": "build", "provider": "go", "target": "project" } } } builder_selection is explicit when build.yaml chose the builder and inferred when detection did. discovery holds each detector's observations and the evidence behind each choice (formatter, linter, package manager and so on). A project with a build.yaml also has an inventory object (undeclared, excluded, tracked, workspaceMembers). --check and --write return a build-inventory record with mode, outcome (for example undeclared), declared, excluded and an undeclared list giving each folder's path, builders and the entry line to add.

Status When 0 Discovery succeeded. With --check, every folder is declared or excluded; with --write, the file was written or nothing was needed 1 --check found an undeclared folder (INVENTORY_UNDECLARED), or --write needs you to choose because several builders recognize one folder 3 build.yaml or oyzu.toml is invalid

Symptom Fix A project you expected is missing Make sure its files are tracked by Git (git add); untracked folders are ignored. Check that its native manifest is at the folder root. A folder is a build by accident (fixtures, examples) List it under exclude: in build.yaml. Needs a choice: several builders recognize one folder Add the build to build.yaml with an explicit uses:. The row shows an example line. No targets found Run from the project root, or pass -C <folder>.
Discovery decisions and build.yaml selectors, including builds build.yaml leaves out. CLI output: project discovery. Set up projects guide.

Three commands for using a project's pinned tools without activating your shell: oyzu exec -- COMMAND runs a command with this project's locked tools first on PATH. oyzu which COMMAND prints the path of the executable the project would use. oyzu env shows the environment Oyzu builds for the project, or prints it as shell assignments. All three use what is locked in oyzu.lock and installed. A command that isn't part of that selection isn't found.
documents.s: oyzu exec, oyzu which and oyzu env

documents.t: oyzu exec [OPTIONS] -- <COMMAND>... Argument Meaning <COMMAND>... Command and arguments to run, written after -- Option Description --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store --offline Use installed tools and cached archives; no network The global options also apply. --toolset NAME runs with that toolset's tools. $ oyzu exec -- go versionCopy go version go1.22.12 windows/amd64 The project pins Go 1.22 in oyzu.toml, so go is the locked 1.22.12 whatever else is on your PATH. Everything after -- goes to the child unchanged, and the child inherits standard input, output and error. oyzu exec exits with the child's exit status. With --json, the child's output is captured and returned in one record: $ oyzu --json exec -- go version { "capture": { "encoding": "utf-8-lossy", "stderr": "pipe", "stdin": "inherited", "stdout": "pipe", "streaming": false, "tty": false }, "exitCode": 0, "invocationId": "58216-1792552148201584600-1", "stderr": "", "stdout": "go version go1.22.12 windows/amd64\n" } capture tells you how the child saw its streams: piped (not a terminal), not streamed live, and decoded as UTF-8 with replacement characters for invalid bytes. Project [env] values and env._.path entries apply to exec only in a trusted folder.

oyzu which [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> Argument Meaning <COMMAND> Command name to look up, such as cargo or node Option Description --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store $ oyzu which goCopy C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\tools\installs\282fe8f8…\payload\bin/go.exe The output is just the path, so it works in scripts: "$(oyzu which go)" version. With --json: {"command":"go","path":"…"}.

oyzu env [OPTIONS] Option Description --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store --shell <SHELL> Print code that applies the environment to this shell instead of describing it: bash, zsh or pwsh

$ oyzu envCopy Project environment ​ Resolved configuration and installed tool environment. Sensitive values are redacted. ​ Effective variables Variable Value GOROOT C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\tools\installs\282fe8f8…\payload GOTOOLCHAIN local ​ PATH (search order) 1. C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\tools\installs\282fe8f8…\payload\bin … ​ Selected executables Command Executable go C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\tools\installs\282fe8f8…\payload\bin/go.exe gofmt C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\tools\installs\282fe8f8…\payload\bin/gofmt.exe ​ Inspection does not change this shell. Enable directory switching with oyzu activate. Output shortened. Values whose names look like credentials (token, secret, password, key and similar) are redacted in this view. It never changes your shell.

eval "$(oyzu env --shell bash)" oyzu env --shell pwsh | Out-String | Invoke-Expression This is a one-time change, with no directory hook and no automatic undo. Use oyzu activate when you want the environment to follow you between projects. Shell code you ask for contains the real values, including any secrets in your configuration.
documents.s: Apply it once to the current shell

documents.t: oyzu --json env returns the same facts as one record: environment (variables, including PATH), executables (command to path), tools (tool to executable), configuration, unset and projectEnvironmentSkipped. projectEnvironmentSkipped is true in an untrusted folder, where project [env] values are shown but not applied by shells, shims and exec. With --shell, --json returns {"shell": …, "script": …}. Evaluate the raw script, never the JSON.

Status When child's status oyzu exec returns the command's own exit status 0 which found the command; env succeeded 1 The command isn't in the selection, or a selected tool isn't installed 4 The lock is missing or stale for a requirement $ oyzu exec -- nosuchcmdCopy ✗ COMMAND_NOT_FOUND: executable is not on PATH Next: Check PATH and the selected tools, or enable automatic installation. $ oyzu which nosuchCopy ✗ COMMAND_FAILED: command is not in the selected closure Code Fix COMMAND_NOT_FOUND Declare and install the tool that provides the command (oyzu install go@1.26), or check the spelling. COMMAND_FAILED: command is not in the selected closure which only finds commands from the project's selected tools. Install the tool that provides it. TOOL_INSTALLATION_MISSING The lock selects a tool that isn't in the store. Run oyzu install. TOOL_LOCK_STALE, TOOL_LOCK_MISSING Run oyzu pin, then oyzu install.
Shell activation, including headless execution and inspection. Tool shell environment. CLI output: JSON results and errors for the exec --json capture fields.

Two read-only commands for looking at builds after they ran. oyzu inspect checks a build's output: every file in the bundle must match the digest the build recorded. oyzu history lists the builds Oyzu keeps and summarizes one of them. Neither runs project code.

oyzu inspect [OPTIONS] [BUNDLE] Argument Meaning [BUNDLE] Bundle directory or OCI archive; defaults to the project's bundle directory (dist/) A bundle is the directory oyzu build writes (dist/ by default: manifest, plan, reports and artifacts), or an exported OCI image archive (.tar). With no argument, Oyzu uses the project's build.bundleDirectory. A bundle path you name is inspected directly, without opening project configuration. Option Description --provenance <FILE> Saved standard Sigstore v0.3 SLSA provenance bundle --release-profile <FILE> Your expected GitHub workflow and source, as an independent profile file --artifact <PATH> Recorded file path inside an Oyzu bundle directory --trusted-root <FILE> A Sigstore root you supply; defaults to the public root built into oyzu The global options also apply.

$ oyzu inspectCopy ✓ Bundle contents verified · build succeeded Run 43456-1792551936872501200 · source sha256:a98b850fd775 · uncommitted changes ​ Targets Target Builder Platform Path project go/app windows/x86_64 . ​ Actions Action Status Exit Gate project:build succeeded 0 required ​ Artifacts Path (under dist/) Kind Size Platform Digest project/windows/x86_64/ file 2.0 MB windows/x86_64 sha256:ed5cb4ccc3e5 project-0.0.0-dev.g1e5ffa22c338.exe ​ Verified: every recorded file matches its digest. This does not show who produced the build or that it may be released. Use --json for the full manifest, including the plan and execution envelope. The header says two separate things: whether the bundle's files check out, and whether the build it records succeeded. A failed build's bundle can still verify.
oyzu inspect path/to/downloaded/dist oyzu inspect image.tar For an OCI archive, the output shows its kind, platforms, size and digests.

A passing inspection shows the files are intact. It doesn't show who built them. To check that, give oyzu inspect a saved Sigstore provenance bundle and a release profile describing the GitHub workflow and source you expect: oyzu inspect app.tar.gz --provenance app.sigstore.json --release-profile expected-build.json oyzu inspect dist --artifact app/linux/x86_64/app \ --provenance app.sigstore.json --release-profile expected-build.json --json For a bundle directory, also name the recorded file with --artifact. Verification runs offline against the saved evidence and never runs the artifact. The ordinary bundle checks run first, and any failure exits non-zero. With --json, the releaseVerification object reports the signature, subject and expectation results separately. A valid signature doesn't establish a SLSA level or permission to publish. See release provenance verification for the profile fields and limits.
oyzu --json inspect returns the full build-manifest record, the same document oyzu --json build prints, plus invocationId, runId, planDigest and envelopeDigest. See oyzu build JSON output.

$ oyzu inspect nosuchdirCopy ✗ COMMAND_FAILED: …\hello\nosuchdir does not exist; a bundle is the dist/ directory written by `oyzu build` or an exported OCI archive Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command. A missing dist/ names where Oyzu looked and suggests oyzu build. A file whose bytes no longer match its digest fails the check and exits non-zero.

oyzu history [OPTIONS] [ID] Argument Meaning [ID] An invocation or run ID from a build's output With no argument it lists retained builds, newest first. With an ID (from the Details line at the end of a build, or from the list) it prints a short summary of that build and where its files are. history has no options beyond the global options.

$ oyzu historyCopy Invocation evidence Invocation / run Outcome Scope Started 56588-1792551984675856100-1 succeeded 1 targets · 1 actions 2026-10-21T03:06:27.150920900+00:00 44556-1792551937713942400-1 succeeded 1 targets · 1 actions 2026-10-21T03:05:40.216374700+00:00 … Next: oyzu history <ID> for a bounded summary and evidence paths Recorded observations; this summary does not verify artifact contents.

$ oyzu history 56588-1792551984675856100-1Copy Invocation evidence Outcome: succeeded Invocation: 56588-1792551984675856100-1 Run: 56588-1792551987150920900 Scope: 1 targets · 1 actions ​ Actions Executed: 1 Checks not requested project: format-check, lint, test ​ Why each stage ran or was reused project:build — Executed Reuse: source files in scope changed (also: action definition: project:build argv, project:build extensions) manifest: …\hello\dist\manifest.json bundle: …\hello\dist events: …\hello\dist\logs\events.jsonl plan: …\hello\dist\plan.json Next: oyzu inspect <bundle-directory> --json for full verified records Output shortened.

oyzu --json history returns an invocation-history record. Each entry in entries has the IDs, status, startedAt, target and artifact counts, action counts (reused, succeededNow, total), and the bundle and manifest paths, plus checks, tests, decisions, reuse, failures and diagnostics.

$ oyzu history 1-2-3Copy ✗ INVOCATION_NOT_FOUND: no retained bundle records this invocation; use oyzu history to see available evidence. Operations ending before a bundle is created and externally removed history are unavailable. This exits 5. History only knows builds whose bundle is still on disk.
Status When 0 Listed, summarized or verified 1 The bundle doesn't exist, a recorded file doesn't match its digest 5 INVOCATION_NOT_FOUND for oyzu history ID
Build bundles and retention, including retained invocation lookup. CLI output: inspecting a build. Release provenance verification. Artifacts, bundles and evidence.

These commands manage which tool versions a project asks for and has locked. Two files work together: oyzu.toml holds what you asked for, as you typed it (go = "1.22"), in the [tools] table. oyzu.lock records the exact version and verified archive for every platform (1.22.12, with URL and SHA-256 per platform). Commit it. Command Changes oyzu.toml Changes oyzu.lock Downloads and installs oyzu pin only with named tools yes no oyzu install (no arguments) no can add missing entries; never with --frozen yes oyzu install TOOL@VERSION yes yes yes, for this machine oyzu update never yes yes, for this machine oyzu uninstall TOOL yes yes no (installed files stay in the store) oyzu reshim no no no (refreshes shims only) Oyzu installs node, npm, pnpm, yarn, go, python, java, maven, gradle, dotnet, rust, zig, helm, kubectl, k3d, liquibase and tailscale, the Cargo helpers cargo-nextest and cargo-llvm-cov, and (experimentally) registry packages from the tool index. oyzu tools info NAME with an unknown name prints the current list. No account is needed. Fully tested on Linux x86-64; Windows x86-64 works with less test coverage. See tool commands for details.
documents.s: oyzu pin, install, update, uninstall and reshim

documents.t: Reads what the project's builds need (from native files such as go.mod, package.json engines or rust-toolchain.toml, and from oyzu.toml), picks concrete versions and records them in oyzu.lock. It never installs anything. oyzu pin [OPTIONS] [TOOL[@VERSION]]... Argument Meaning [TOOL[@VERSION]]... Declare and lock these tools without installing (omit for discovered requirements) Option Description --dry-run Preview discovered requirements and lock changes without writing files --refresh Refresh installation recipes while keeping the selected tool versions --offline Resolve from existing locks and cached metadata only; no network access $ oyzu pin --dry-runCopy Build requirements · preview ​ Consolidated across 1 build target(s). ​ Tool requirements Requirement Requested version Needed for Installation support Applies to oyzu:go 1.22 Declared requirement Oyzu All targets … No files changed. Tool resolution complete. Installed availability was not checked. Nothing was installed. Use --json for sources, constraints and discovery limitations. Without --dry-run, the last line becomes Tool resolutions pinned. and oyzu.lock is written. Named tools (oyzu pin kubectl@1.34 helm@3.22.0) are also declared in oyzu.toml; you can't combine them with --refresh or --offline. Plain oyzu pin also locks every toolset; oyzu --toolset NAME pin locks only that toolset. oyzu --json pin returns the requirements, requested_versions, proposed_files, platform compiler_metadata, diagnostics and complete. If resolution is incomplete, it exits 1.

oyzu install [OPTIONS] [TOOLS]... Argument Meaning [TOOLS]... Tools to declare and install, as [provider:]name[@version] (omit to install everything declared). Without a version, a declared tool keeps its requirement and an undeclared one takes the newest eligible version Option Description -g, --global Act on your global (user) configuration and its lock instead of the project --local Act on oyzu.local.toml; the lock stays the project's --dry-run With tools: report what would be declared, resolved and locked, and write nothing --frozen Require an existing matching lock; don't resolve new versions --offline Use only existing locks, installations and cached archives --update [<UPDATE>...] Deprecated alias for oyzu update --artifact-set <FILE> A resolved artifact set (JSON) that supplies a registry tool (oyzu:NAME@VERSION); repeatable. Without --artifact-set-digest, the set is local and you vouch for it --artifact-set-digest <sha256:DIGEST> Pin a set record by its digests.full; repeatable (provisional flag) --connector-bindings <CONNECTOR_BINDINGS> Host-owned connector endpoints and authorization environment references --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store Version forms: go@1.26 is a prefix, go@1.26.8 is exact, go@latest is the newest eligible version, and plain go keeps an existing declaration (or takes the newest when undeclared).

On a fresh clone, this is the one command a teammate needs: $ oyzu installCopy Installing tools Checking pinned tools and verifying reusable installations Tool installation ​ Tool Version Result go 1.22.12 reused ​ Selected installations verified. Use oyzu tools current to inspect availability. In CI, use oyzu install --frozen: it fails instead of resolving anything new when the lock doesn't match.

Preview first, then apply: $ oyzu install go@1.22 --dry-runCopy Installing requested tools Resolving every platform, then installing this one Dry run · no files were changed ✓ Would install go 1.22.12 Would declare "1.22" in …\hello\oyzu.toml (project) Locked in …\hello\oyzu.lock for 4 platforms (darwin/arm64/native, linux/amd64/gnu, linux/arm64/gnu, windows/amd64/msvc) ​ Store: C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\tools No archive was downloaded and no file was written. Run again without --dry-run to apply. oyzu install go@1.22 Oyzu resolves every platform in the lock but downloads only this machine's archive. The configuration and the lock are written together: if anything fails, both stay unchanged. Several tools in one command are applied together or not at all.
documents.s: Add a tool to the project

documents.t: Flag Configuration written Lock none, inside a project project oyzu.toml (created if absent) project oyzu.lock -g, --global your user configuration the oyzu.lock beside it --local oyzu.local.toml project oyzu.lock --toolset NAME that toolset's [toolsets.NAME.tools] that toolset's entries in oyzu.lock oyzu install -g node@22 # your default Node for every project Outside a project, the project scope fails with TOOL_NO_PROJECT instead of guessing.

Moves each locked version forward within its existing requirement. update never edits oyzu.toml; to change the requirement itself, run oyzu install tool@new-version. oyzu update [OPTIONS] [TOOLS]... Argument Meaning [TOOLS]... Tools to update (omit to update every tool in the selected scope) Option Description -g, --global Act on your global (user) configuration and its lock instead of the project --local Act on oyzu.local.toml; the lock stays the project's --dry-run Report the versions that would be locked and write nothing --connector-bindings <CONNECTOR_BINDINGS> Host-owned connector endpoints and authorization environment references --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store $ oyzu update --dry-runCopy Updating tools Resolving newer versions within each requirement Dry run · no files were changed ✓ Checked 1 tool ​ Tool Requirement Was Now Result go 1.22 1.22.12 1.22.12 current

Removes a tool's declaration and its lock entries at one scope. Installed files stay in the shared store, because other projects may use them. oyzu uninstall [OPTIONS] <TOOLS>... Argument Meaning <TOOLS>... Tools to remove, by name Option Description -g, --global Act on your global (user) configuration and its lock instead of the project --local Act on oyzu.local.toml; the lock stays the project's --dry-run Report what would be removed and write nothing --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store $ oyzu uninstall go --dry-runCopy Dry run · no files were changed ✓ Would remove go Declaration "1.22" removed from …\hello\oyzu.toml (project) Lock entry removed from …\hello\oyzu.lock ​ Installed files stay in the store and remain listed by oyzu tools list as unreferenced. A tool that comes only from a native file (such as go.mod) and isn't declared in oyzu.toml fails with TOOL_NOT_DECLARED, and no files change.

Refreshes the shims folder (small launchers named after each installed tool's commands) and any existing activation launchers. It downloads nothing and doesn't edit your shell profile. oyzu reshim [OPTIONS] Option Description --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store The reported folder belongs on PATH for IDEs, scheduled tasks and other non-interactive programs; each shim works out the project it runs in. oyzu shell install puts it there persistently (your user Path on Windows), and the install scripts run it for you. On Windows, install both oyzu.exe and oyzu-shim.exe. With only oyzu.exe, reshim (and the shims step of oyzu install) fails with missing native launcher …\oyzu-shim.exe; install both Oyzu binaries.

Status When 0 Success, including dry runs 1 Resolution or installation failed (for example, an unknown tool name or an unreachable publisher), or pin couldn't resolve everything 2 Invalid arguments, such as a tool spec with --frozen (TOOL_FLAGS_CONFLICT) or a spec that can't be parsed 3 tools.allowed or policy refuses the tool, or a version is below a native minimum (TOOL_NATIVE_MINIMUM_CONFLICT) 4 The lock is missing or stale (TOOL_LOCK_MISSING, TOOL_LOCK_STALE) 5 TOOL_NOT_DECLARED or TOOL_NO_PROJECT

$ oyzu install nosuchtool@1 --dry-runCopy ✗ TOOL_NAME_UNKNOWN: nosuchtool is not a known short name (catalog 2026.10.5); name the package explicitly, for example oyzu:<owner>/<repo> Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command. Code Fix TOOL_FLAGS_CONFLICT Tool specs resolve online, so --frozen, --offline and --update only work without them. Run two commands. TOOL_NAME_UNKNOWN, TOOL_ALIAS_UNSUPPORTED Use a supported name (oyzu tools info NAME lists them) or a full registry name. TOOL_LOCK_STALE The lock has no pin for a requirement, often after go.mod or package.json changed. Run oyzu pin, then oyzu install. PIN_EDIT_CONFLICT, CONFIG_EDIT_CONFLICT Another process edited the files at the same time. Retry. PIN_RECOVERY_REQUIRED An interrupted edit left a journal. Run oyzu install or oyzu pin in that folder to recover.
Tool commands: scopes, specs, results and errors in full. Configuration: toolsets. Tool index and organization tool catalog. Manage your first tool guide.

Write or check OS package locks for Docker targets. For each Docker target, oyzu lock builds every stage that contributes to the image once, compares the stage's package database with its base image's, and records each newly installed Debian or Alpine package (URL, version, checksum and Package URL) in debs.lock.yaml or apks.lock.yaml next to the Dockerfile. It never parses the RUN shell. Commit the lock with your change, and don't edit it by hand. Once a lock exists, oyzu build installs from it: RUN steps see only a local repository that serves the locked files. Tool versions are locked by oyzu pin, not by this command. oyzu lock [OPTIONS] Note: OS package locks are experimental and need a Docker engine with BuildKit (docker buildx). See OS package locks for limits.

Option Description --check Write nothing; exit non-zero if a lock is missing or stale --update [<SELECTOR>...] Re-observe with fresh base image digests and no build cache. Optional selectors name a target or a lock path; none means every lock --inputs List every locked package and base image for Renovate; resolves nothing --store <DIR> Use this tool store (which also holds installed plugins) instead of the shared user store The global options also apply.

oyzu lock # write missing locks and regenerate stale ones oyzu lock --check # fail if any lock is missing or stale; writes nothing oyzu lock --update # re-observe every lock with fresh bases and no build cache oyzu lock --update api # re-observe only the api target's locks oyzu lock --inputs --json # list locked packages for Renovate; resolves nothing A lock that is already current is left alone. In a project with no Docker target that installs OS packages, it prints No Docker target installs OS packages; there is nothing to lock. --check works offline and fits a CI step: it fails when a Dockerfile change installs a package the lock doesn't cover. A tag in FROM keeps the digest already in the lock until you run --update.

--json returns one record with mode (write, update, check or inputs) and outcome (written or current for writes, current or stale for --check, listed for --inputs). Each --check entry has a status (current, stale or missing) and, when not current, code: OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE and fix: oyzu lock. --inputs entries list each base image and package in the form Renovate reads.

Status When 0 Locks written or already current; --check found every lock current 1 An operational error, such as a failed observation build 2 Invalid arguments 3 Configuration or policy validation failed 4 --check found a missing or stale lock

Code Fix OS_PACKAGE_LOCK_STALE Run oyzu lock and commit the result. OS_PACKAGE_UNRESOLVABLE A package was installed from a file, or its version disappeared upstream. Install from a configured repository, or run oyzu lock again. OS_PACKAGE_UNVERIFIED apt reported a signature problem. Fix the repository's signing key in the image. OS_PACKAGE_NOT_LOCKED A RUN step asked for a package the lock doesn't contain. Run oyzu lock --update, or remove the install. OS_PACKAGE_UPDATE_SELECTOR --update can't select a single package. Update the whole lock or its target.
OS package locks: how it works, frozen builds, JSON shape and limits. Docker images.

Builders run as plugins: separate programs that Oyzu starts for each build. A plugin is a package such as oyzu/go, and the name you write as uses: in build.yaml (for example go/app) is a reference to one of its profiles. Use oyzu plugins to find plugins, see which one each target of your project uses and why, and update the selections recorded in oyzu.lock. oyzu plugins [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> Subcommand What it does search [QUERY] Browse or search the references the catalogs offer versions <REFERENCE> Show a reference's known releases and why each can or cannot be selected here info <REFERENCE[@VERSION]> Show a release's package, platforms, download routes and verification list List the plugin releases installed in the plugin store current Show this project's locked plugin selections, whether they are installed, and whether they can run here explain [TARGET] Explain which plugin a target uses and why, with the ways to change it update [REFERENCE[@SELECTOR]]... Update locked selections within their adopted major version prune SHA256... Preview, then remove, installed copies of revoked releases search, versions, info, list, current and explain only read: the cached catalog, the plugin store and oyzu.lock. They never download or start a plugin, run a project tool or change a file. Only --refresh updates the cached catalog. update changes oyzu.lock, and prune --apply deletes installed copies. Note: Plugins are experimental. Releases published so far are previews. To let builds use previews, opt in once for your user account: oyzu config set --global plugins.preview true. A project file cannot do this, because the release is code that runs on your machine.

For each target, oyzu build looks for a plugin in this order and uses the first match: A local development binding in your user configuration (see Develop a builder locally). A plugins.packages binding in your user configuration. The release already recorded in oyzu.lock. Locked releases are replayed, never replaced by a newer catalog entry. The newest eligible release in the plugin catalog. The first oyzu build that picks a plugin from the catalog downloads it, verifies its signature and digests, installs it in the shared tool store and writes the choice to oyzu.lock. Commit the lock so everyone builds with the same release. Other commands (build --plan, run, discover) never download or install; they replay the lock. If no plugin matches, the build stops with PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE and says why. There is no built-in fallback.

All inspection subcommands (search, versions, info, list, current, explain) take: Option Description --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store --refresh Update the verified catalog cache from permitted sources first. Installs no plugin --offline Never use the network. Read only the verified cached catalog search also takes --type <TYPE>, which shows only plugins that serve one capability. The only value today is build. update takes --dry-run, --store and --offline. The global options apply to all subcommands.

Lists the references the catalogs offer. $ oyzu plugins search --offlineCopy 2 plugin references in the catalog ​ Reference Package Latest stable Build selects Status go/app oyzu/go (build) — — unavailable: preview only go/library oyzu/go (build) — — unavailable: preview only ​ About go/app Build, test and package Go modules and workspaces with the native go toolchain. official default · official catalog serial 21 · publisher oyzu go/library Test and vet Go library modules without producing an executable. official default · official catalog serial 21 · publisher oyzu ​ Inspect one with oyzu plugins versions <reference> or oyzu plugins info <reference>[@v<major>]. Output shortened. "unavailable: preview only" means the only release is a preview and you have not opted in. Search covers the official catalog and your organization's catalog. It does not crawl OCI registries, so a plugin you reference explicitly can work without being listed. Eligibility is judged for this machine only.

versions lists a reference's known releases and why each can or cannot be selected on this machine. info shows one release in detail. The selector can be a major version (@v0) or an exact version (@0.1.0). $ oyzu plugins versions go/app --offlineCopy 1 known release of go/app · oyzu/go (official default) ​ Locked here nothing: this project has not adopted this reference ​ Version Labels Selectable here Release 0.1.0-preview.1 (preview) no: preview only sha256:25f830bd…f9bf ​ Preview releases are selectable only with: oyzu config set --global plugins.preview true Output shortened. latest-stable is the newest stable release even if it cannot run here. latest-compatible is the newest that fits your Oyzu version and platform. update-candidate is what plugins update would move to inside the adopted major version. adoption-candidate is what the next oyzu build would adopt. $ oyzu plugins info go/app --offlineCopy go/app 0.1.0-preview.1 · oyzu/go (build) ​ Build, test and package Go modules and workspaces with the native go toolchain. ​ Release Publisher oyzu Source official default · official catalog serial 21 Status not selectable here: preview only Release sha256:25f830bd740620e6a54a5eac922d1a9505e12f1e1db732f8538152447ba1f9bf Profiles app (builder), library (builder) ​ Platforms Platform Size Payload linux/amd64-musl 408.9 KiB sha256:de17b89e…9dba windows/amd64-msvc 278.3 KiB sha256:0127cd09…d48a … ​ Verification Metadata verified signed catalog The catalog metadata is verified. Package bytes are verified when installed; this view downloads none. Output shortened.

Lists the plugin releases installed in the plugin store: package, version, the references it serves, platforms, whether this project locks it, and its release digest. It lists the store only. The store keeps no record of which projects use a release.

oyzu plugins current [OPTIONS] oyzu plugins explain [OPTIONS] [TARGET] Argument Meaning [TARGET] A target, by name or path. Omit it for every plugin-backed target current shows each locked selection with its install state and whether it can run here. explain prints the same Selection record oyzu build prints: which release, why it was chosen and how to change it. $ oyzu plugins explain --offlineCopy No target here uses a plugin ​ No package-backed target is selected. Declare uses: <reference> in build.yaml or supply the required admitted package; find catalog entries with oyzu plugins search.

oyzu plugins update [OPTIONS] [REFERENCE[@SELECTOR]]... Argument / option Description [REFERENCE[@SELECTOR]]... References to update, each optionally with @v<major>, @<version> or @sha256:<digest>. Omit it to update every locked selection --dry-run Check everything and show the lock change without writing oyzu.lock --store <DIR> Use this tool store instead of the shared user store --offline Never use the network. Update from the cached catalog only oyzu plugins update # every locked selection, within its major version oyzu plugins update go/app@v2 # adopt major version 2 explicitly oyzu plugins update go/app@1.4.2 # select exactly 1.4.2 oyzu plugins update go/app@sha256:… # restore one exact release (the undo line a build prints) oyzu plugins update --dry-run A routine update moves to the newest eligible release inside the adopted major version. It never goes to an older release or to a preview. Each new release is installed and verified first, and oyzu.lock is rewritten only if every requested selection passes, in one step. A withdrawn or revoked release, or an unusable catalog, fails without changing the lock. With no plugin locked: $ oyzu plugins update --dry-run --offlineCopy oyzu.lock selects no plugin; nothing to update ​ Lock …\hello\oyzu.lock (unchanged) ​ Nothing was launched and no file changed.

oyzu plugins prune [--store DIR] [--apply] SHA256... When a release is revoked, Oyzu refuses to run it but leaves its files in the store. prune removes them. Copy exact sha256: release digests from plugins list or plugins info. Without --apply it only shows what it would do. --apply rechecks the cached catalog and the installation, then removes each selected revoked copy that no running Oyzu is using. It never refreshes the catalog or downloads anything. Run oyzu plugins list --refresh first if you need current revocations. An expired catalog, an ordinary withdrawal or an unavailable source cannot authorize deletion. Copies in use, and installations Oyzu cannot inspect, are kept. Project locks are not changed. A copy with no active user may still be locked by some project, so update that project with oyzu plugins update. Each release gets a state (eligible, retained, removed, absent or incomplete) with a reason. Preview exits 0. --apply exits 1 if anything was retained or removal was incomplete. If a filesystem error interrupts a removal, a partial copy can remain; check the reason and the leftover files before retrying. There is no option to remove everything or to force removal. $ oyzu plugins prune sha256:e6338a15… --store ~/storeCopy Plugin cleanup preview Release State Reason sha256:e6338a15a12b6442cf52… eligible Revoked release has no active cooperative use lease and is eligible for explicit removal. Store ~/store Catalog acme catalog serial 2 No installation was removed. Repeat the exact selected digests with --apply to recheck eligibility and remove revoked copies without active use leases. Output shortened.

You can bind a compiled plugin you built yourself to a profile that has no packaged plugin. Put the binding in user or machine configuration, never in the project, and select the same short id in build.yaml. The names and path here are examples. The executable must implement the builder operations for your project. User or machine configuration [plugins.development] "independent/app" = "/absolute/path/to/independent-plugin" build.yaml builds: app: uses: independent/app oyzu build app The build runs on the host and collects the artifacts the plugin declares. Oyzu still resolves the tools the plugin asks for through your normal configuration, lock, tool policy and offline rules. A local binding does not add zero-config detection, with options, dependency preparation or isolated execution.
