The other checks still ran. Because the build failed, Oyzu kept the program from your last successful build. Change "Hi, " back to "Hello, " and the build passes again.
documents.s: 7. Break something and read the failure

documents.t: Command What it does oyzu discover Shows the targets Oyzu detected and which builder handles each, without running project code oyzu run list Lists the tasks Oyzu found and the command each runs oyzu build --plan Previews stages and tool needs without running anything oyzu build --full Builds, tests, lints and format-checks; writes dist/ and oyzu.lock oyzu history Lists past builds oyzu inspect dist Checks the output bundle against its recorded digests

Lock and share tool versions with your team: Manage your tools. Bring Oyzu to a real repository: Adopt Oyzu in an existing repository. Your language: Rust, Node applications or Go. What is in dist/: build bundles.

Oyzu skips work that hasn't changed by reusing earlier results from its action cache. You can ask why any stage ran, and share results between machines through an OCI registry. You need: nothing for the local cache; it is on by default. A remote cache needs an OCI registry you control.

Each stage gets a key from everything it depends on: builder and version, platform, tool versions, dependencies, the stage's command and settings, the target's source files, and earlier outputs it uses. When a key matches a stored result, Oyzu restores the outputs, checks their digests and skips the command. Reused work is always labelled. A restored test report shows as reused test evidence, not run now.

oyzu build oyzu build # nothing changed $ oyzu build # second run, nothing changedCopy … ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── · api · windows/x86_64 Reused from an earlier run · not executed now · originally ran 2026-10-21T03:17:54Z (key ca4ede1b38ee) 00:03 ↺ api build reused was 1.1s · worker · windows/x86_64 Reused from an earlier run · not executed now · originally ran 2026-10-21T03:17:54Z (key bbc60dc10ed2) 00:03 ↺ worker build reused was 1.3s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── api/ api dist/api/windows/x86_64/api-0.0.0-dev.g638adc2c9cc7.exe 2.0 MB development worker/ worker dist/worker/windows/x86_64/worker-0.0.0-dev.ge3334bd9de96.exe 2.0 MB development Checks not requested api: format-check, lint, test Checks not requested worker: format-check, lint, test ​ ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 2 reused · 3.6s api/ ✓ 1 target 1.1s worker/ ✓ 1 target 1.3s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 40628-1792552775870869400-1

Edit a file in worker/ and build with --explain: $ oyzu build --explainCopy … ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 1 executed · 1 reused · 4.9s api/ ✓ 1 target 1.1s worker/ ✓ 1 target 1.2s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 57240-1792552779758664800-1 ​ Why each stage ran or was reused api:build — Reused Recorded selection: api (selected) Reuse: a stored result matches this key (run 7212-1792552671925578400, 2026-10-21T03:17:54Z) Source detail unavailable: file-level membership of the effective target scope is unavailable Producing run: 7212-1792552671925578400 worker:build — Executed Recorded selection: worker (selected) Reuse: source files in scope changed (also: action definition: worker:build argv, worker:build extensions) Source detail unavailable: file-level membership of the effective target scope is unavailable Each entry names the first part of the key that changed since that stage last ran. To ask about one target without building: $ oyzu cache explain workerCopy Cache key explanation worker ​ worker (whole target) Key de88ec5f061b · since run 57240-1792552783009968100 · last seen run 57240-1792552783009968100 (2026-10-21T03:19:43Z) Result stored · the next build with these inputs reuses it Changed since run 40628-1792552779260479100: source files in scope changed (also: action definition: worker:build argv, worker:build extensions) ​ Keys come from the toolchain, dependencies, stage definition, source in scope and consumed outputs. Use `oyzu build --explain` to see this for every stage of a build. The same answers are kept with each build: oyzu history <invocation-id> shows up to eight of them.
documents.s: 2. Change one target and ask why

documents.t: $ oyzu cache statusCopy Action cache ​ Location C:\Users\you\AppData\Local\Oyzu\cache\actions (default per-user location) Entries 552 results · 2841 blobs Size 9.9 GiB of 10.0 GiB retention budget Docker 5 images · 2.6 GiB of 20.0 GiB image budget (cache.dockerMaxMiB) Local use enabled ​ Reuse is local to this user and machine. Ephemeral CI runners start empty; shared caching is a later milestone. Use `oyzu cache clear` to empty it, or `oyzu build --no-cache` to bypass it once. To Run or set Run everything once, without reading or writing the cache oyzu build --no-cache Turn the local cache off cache.local = false Empty the cache (bundles in dist/ are untouched) oyzu cache clear Check that confined stages declare every file they read oyzu build --verify-contract (reuses and stores nothing) The cache is per user and shared across projects: Platform Location Windows %LocalAppData%\Oyzu\cache\actions macOS ~/Library/Caches/Oyzu/actions Linux $XDG_CACHE_HOME/oyzu/actions, else ~/.cache/oyzu/actions Set cache.dir in user or system configuration to move it. Above 10 GiB, the least recently used results are removed at the end of a build. oyzu cache clear fails while a build is using the cache; don't delete store.lock, just retry.
documents.s: 3. Inspect, skip or clear the cache

documents.t: Some work always runs, and the output says why: Targets with your own tasks or stage replacements, unless they set cache = true and declare outputs. Targets with hooks that declare no outputs. oyzu history reports contains authored tasks or hooks without declared outputs, which are never cached by default. Targets that use secret environment values. Tasks run directly with oyzu run. Failed, blocked or cancelled targets. Their results are never stored. Optimized and development builds never share results, and upgrading Oyzu starts the cache fresh. A damaged entry is set aside and the stage runs. An unusable cache location never fails a build.

Note: The remote cache is experimental and supported on Linux. It has been tested with zot, CNCF Distribution behind a token service, and a Harbor proxy-cache project. A remote cache lets one machine reuse results another pushed to an OCI registry repository. Entries are checked against their digests before use. cache.remote and cache.ciRemote are refused in project files, so a checkout can't redirect your cache. Set them in user configuration or the environment: export OYZU_CACHE_REMOTE=oci://registry.example.com/team/oyzu-cache # read on a local miss # user configuration (oyzu config set --global …) [cache] remote = "oci://registry.example.com/team/oyzu-cache" write = true # also push results this machine builds (off by default) Setting Default Meaning cache.remote / OYZU_CACHE_REMOTE unset Repository to read from after a local miss, and to write to when cache.write is on cache.ciRemote / OYZU_CACHE_CI_REMOTE unset A repository only CI writes to (see below) cache.write false Push results to the remote cache.immutableTags false Set only for a registry that refuses to replace tags OYZU_CACHE_TOKEN unset Registry token. Only from the environment, never a setting A localhost registry uses HTTP; everything else uses HTTPS with your proxy and CA settings.
documents.s: 4. Share results through a remote OCI cache (experimental)

documents.t: # in CI export OYZU_CACHE_CI_REMOTE=oci://registry.example.com/team/oyzu-cache/ci Build Reads (after a local miss) Writes (with cache.write) In CI (a CI provider is detected) cache.ciRemote only cache.ciRemote Anywhere else cache.ciRemote, then cache.remote cache.remote only The registry must refuse writes without the CI credential; that is what makes the CI repository trustworthy. Oyzu doesn't sign cache entries. Remote problems never fail a build: A 404 is a cache miss. Repeated 5xx errors or timeouts turn the remote off for the rest of the build. A 401 or 403 does the same after one token renewal. The summary line adds remote counts, for example remote 7 reused · 0 pushed. Entries larger than 256 MiB are not pushed. Details: remote OCI cache.
documents.s: A CI-only repository that developers read

documents.t: Symptom Cause and fix Everything always runs Run oyzu build --explain. Common causes: a hook without outputs, a changed oyzu.toml (configuration is part of every key), a new Oyzu version, or --no-cache. One target never reuses oyzu history <id> gives the reason, for example hooks or secret environment values. cache clear says the cache is busy A build is running. Retry after it finishes. The remote never hits Set cache.remote in user configuration or OYZU_CACHE_REMOTE; project files are refused. In CI only cache.ciRemote is read. Remote pushes are refused The token is read-only or missing. The build still succeeds and records why nothing was pushed. Reference: action cache, explaining reuse. Concept: caching and reuse.

Run the same oyzu build in CI that you run locally. CI builds run every check with the tools in oyzu.lock and leave a bundle you can keep as a job artifact. No account or CI plugin is needed. You need: a repository that already builds locally with Oyzu (Adopt Oyzu), with oyzu.lock committed.

Oyzu detects the CI provider from its standard environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TF_BUILD, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CIRCLECI and about twenty more; any enabled CI variable also counts). That sets the build context: Context When Checks that run local No CI detected Only checks set to required (a fast build) ci A CI provider is detected Every check that isn't off: tests, lint, format check pr A pull or merge request (on GitHub: GITHUB_BASE_REF is set) Every check that isn't off release A tag build (on GitHub: GITHUB_REF_TYPE=tag) Every check that isn't off, plus your [context.release] settings So CI needs no extra flags. Here is a build with GITHUB_ACTIONS=true in a repository with two Go targets: $ GITHUB_ACTIONS=true oyzu buildCopy Building shop windows/x86_64 (host) · local · CI · GitHub Actions (unverified) · context ci · full ::group::Oyzu Preparation ​ ── Prepare ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── … ::endgroup:: ✓ Tools 1 tool pinned · 0 installed now 3.2s go 1.22.12 already installed detected from go.mod ​ … ── Plan ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 2 targets format lint test build pre_build needs api/ api run run run run - worker/ worker run run run run run api · format-check ​ profile api and worker · development · local dist only ​ ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 00:05 .. api build started 00:06 ✓ api build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false… executed 1.3s 00:06 .. api test started 00:09 ✓ api test go test -json -coverprofile=C:\Use… executed 2.2s 00:09 .. api lint started 00:10 still running: api lint 0s · 6 waiting 00:10 ✓ api lint go vet ./... executed 1.2s 00:10 .. api format-check started 00:10 ✓ api format-check gofmt -l . executed 0.2s 00:10 .. worker pre_build started 00:11 ✓ worker pre_build go vet ./... executed 1.2s 00:11 .. worker build started 00:13 ✓ worker build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false… executed 1.3s 00:13 .. worker test started 00:15 ✓ worker test go test -json -coverprofile=C:\Use… executed 2.1s 00:15 .. worker lint started 00:16 ✓ worker lint go vet ./... executed 1.2s 00:16 .. worker format-check started 00:16 ✓ worker format-check gofmt -l . executed <0.1s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── api/ api dist/api/windows/x86_64/api-0.0.0-dev.g638adc2c9cc7.exe 2.0 MB development worker/ worker dist/worker/windows/x86_64/worker-0.0.0-dev.ge3334bd9de96.exe 2.0 MB development ​ Checks selected 6 actions · 6 succeeded ​ Tests run now 2 passed · 0 failed · 0 skipped (2 collected reports) Coverage api: 50.0% (1/2 statements) Coverage worker: 50.0% (1/2 statements) ​ ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 9 executed · 17.1s api/ ✓ 1 target 4.9s worker/ ✓ 1 target 5.9s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 16232-1792552806550250500-1 Output shortened. ::group:: lines fold the preparation steps in the GitHub Actions log, and long actions print still running lines. The detected context only chooses checks; it never grants permission to publish or trust a cache, hence (unverified). To set the context yourself, pass --context ci or set OYZU_CONTEXT=release (for a manual release job with no tag). Under a detected CI provider you can raise the context but not lower it.

Use the install script in the job, or preinstall oyzu and oyzu-shim in your runner image. Pin a release with OYZU_VERSION so every job uses the same Oyzu. While the release repository is private, the script needs a GitHub token that can read it in GH_TOKEN.

Save this as .github/workflows/build.yml. It expects a repository variable OYZU_VERSION (an Oyzu release tag) and a secret OYZU_RELEASES_TOKEN (a token that can read Oyzu releases). name: build on: pull_request: push: branches: [main] permissions: contents: read jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 timeout-minutes: 60 steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 # --affected needs the base commit locally - name: Install oyzu env: OYZU_VERSION: ${{ vars.OYZU_VERSION }} GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OYZU_RELEASES_TOKEN }} run: | curl -fsSL https://docs.oyzu.ai/install.sh | sh echo "$HOME/.oyzu/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH" - name: Restore installed tools uses: actions/cache@v4 with: path: ~/.local/share/oyzu/tools key: oyzu-tools-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('oyzu.lock') }} - name: Check that every project is declared if: hashFiles('build.yaml') != '' run: oyzu discover --check - name: Build what the pull request changed if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' run: oyzu build --affected "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" - name: Build everything if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' run: oyzu build - name: Verify the bundle run: oyzu inspect - name: Keep the bundle if: always() uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: oyzu-dist path: dist if-no-files-found: ignore How it works: Checks: the job is detected as pr or ci, so tests, lint and format checks run without --full. Tools: oyzu build installs the tools in oyzu.lock, checking each download's digest. Caching ~/.local/share/oyzu/tools saves the downloads. A missing lock entry fails the build. Pull requests: --affected origin/<base> builds changed targets and their dependents, or everything when it can't narrow safely. See Monorepos and affected builds. Output: dist/ is uploaded even when the build fails, so you can read the failure log. Docker: not needed for host builders (Go, Rust, Node applications, Python wheels). Isolated builds, Docker images and --all-platforms need it; see Isolated builds. On Windows runners use install.ps1, and the tool store is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Oyzu\tools. On macOS it is ~/Library/Application Support/Oyzu/tools.

The same steps work on any runner with a POSIX shell. Put oyzu on PATH as in step 1, then: #!/bin/sh set -eu oyzu --version # record which Oyzu ran if [ -f build.yaml ]; then oyzu discover --check; fi if [ -n "${BASE_REF:-}" ]; then # set by your pipeline for merge requests git fetch origin "$BASE_REF" oyzu build --affected "origin/$BASE_REF" else oyzu build fi oyzu inspect Keep dist/ as the job artifact. If Oyzu doesn't recognize your CI system, set CI=true so the build runs every check. Pull-request and tag builds are also recognized on GitLab, Azure Pipelines, CircleCI, Buildkite, Travis CI, Bitbucket Pipelines, Drone, AppVeyor and Jenkins (build context).

With --json, the result goes to standard output and diagnostics to standard error as JSON Lines: oyzu --json build > build-result.json oyzu --json inspect > inspection.json A failed command still returns JSON, with error, code, exitCode and nextStep: $ oyzu --json build nope { "code": "COMMAND_FAILED", "error": "unknown build target nope; available targets: api, worker", "exitCode": 1, "invocationId": "38300-1792552823921616500-1", "nextStep": "Correct the reported cause and retry the command." } Use the exit status to decide what to do: Exit Meaning 0 Succeeded 1 The build or command failed (a failing test, an unknown target) 2 Invalid invocation (unknown flag, invalid platform name) 3 Wrong runner or toolchain: a selected target needs Docker and this runner has none (NEEDS_DOCKER_DAEMON), user namespaces are unavailable, or a configured tool is below a native minimum. Requeue on a suitable runner or fix the configuration 4 --slice build: a needed upstream result is not in the cache (UPSTREAM_NOT_CACHED) 5 --slice build: writing the handoff repository failed (HANDOFF_PUSH_FAILED)

Share results between jobs and runners: set OYZU_CACHE_CI_REMOTE to an OCI repository only CI can write to, cache.write = true in the runner's user configuration, and a registry token in OYZU_CACHE_TOKEN. See Cache build results. One job per platform: oyzu build --plan --json includes a matrix for targets that declare platforms. See a CI matrix from the plan. Limit parallel work on small runners with --jobs N (or OYZU_BUILD_JOBS). Publish artifacts from a release job: Publish artifacts.

Symptom Fix Tests and lint don't run in CI Oyzu didn't detect CI. Set CI=true or pass --context ci. --affected always builds everything The base commit isn't in the clone. Use fetch-depth: 0, or git fetch origin <base> first. TOOL_LOCK_STALE A native file now asks for a version the lock doesn't have. Run oyzu pin locally and commit oyzu.lock. NEEDS_DOCKER_DAEMON (exit 3) A selected target needs Docker. Use a runner with a Docker engine. discover --check fails with INVENTORY_UNDECLARED A folder holds a project that build.yaml neither lists nor excludes. Add it to builds: or exclude:. Passes locally, fails in CI CI runs every check. Reproduce locally with oyzu build --full. More: Troubleshooting. Reference: configuration: local and CI execution context, CLI output, build bundles, build logging.

An isolated build runs each action in a container, from a snapshot of your source, with no network. Use it when builds must not depend on what is installed on the machine. By default, supported builders run directly on your machine (the host path), which is faster. Note: Isolated builds are experimental and supported on Linux hosts. You need: a Docker engine that oyzu can reach and the base execution image, which every builder shares; Oyzu pulls it by pinned digest on first use. Oyzu mounts the engine, the builder's plugin and the tools in oyzu.lock into it; pass --image <manager>=<image> to use an image of your own instead.

Host path (default) Isolated path (--isolated) Where actions run Processes on your machine, with the pinned tools Containers from the execution image, one private workspace per target Source Your working tree A read-only snapshot of it Network during actions Whatever the native tool does None; dependencies are downloaded before the build starts Needs Only the pinned tools Docker (or the crun sandbox for Node on Linux), the execution image and the tools in oyzu.lock Platforms This machine, or a cross toolchain (Rust) What the image builds, or every declared platform with --all-platforms Go applications, Rust, Node applications and Python wheels use the host path by default; Docker images always use a container. oyzu build --plan shows where each target runs.

$ oyzu build api --isolated --planCopy Planning shop Windows x86_64 (host) · Isolated · context local · Fast build requested ​ Build preview Execution: isolated · No tools installed, dependencies downloaded or build actions run. ​ api · go/app · unresolved until executor selection Executor: captured-worker Profile: development · local dist only (no difference: the Go compiler always optimizes) Placement: runs on any platform · Docker engine required · Isolated steps run in the captured worker on a Docker engine Stage Selection Details build selected Native commands and report bindings resolve during preparation format-check skipped fast local build lint skipped fast local build test skipped fast local build prepare unresolved Target environment setup is determined by native dependency preparation package unresolved Artifact packaging is determined by native metadata ​ … Output shortened. A host preview says Executor: host instead. Previews need neither Docker nor images.

oyzu build --isolated # this machine's platform, in containers oyzu build --isolated --image go=<image> # on an image of your own oyzu build --all-platforms # every platform build.yaml declares, in containers --all-platforms is strict: if any declared platform can't be built here, the build fails before anything runs. Container and host results are cached separately, so one never stands in for the other.

In oyzu.toml you can say which executor builds each platform, per folder and per context: [build.executors] "linux/arm64" = "cross-toolchain" # always cross-compiled "darwin/arm64" = "host" # only on a macOS arm64 runner [context.release.build.executors] "linux/x86_64" = "container" # release builds use containers A declared executor is the only one used. If it isn't available, that platform isn't built and the plan says why. See platforms and executors.

On runners with no Docker engine (for example Kubernetes pods), add --no-docker or set OYZU_NO_DOCKER=1, and Oyzu never contacts Docker. If a selected target needs Docker, the build stops before running anything, with exit status 3 so the runner can requeue the job: $ oyzu build api --isolated --no-dockerCopy Building shop windows/x86_64 (host) · isolated · context local · fast ✗ NEEDS_DOCKER_DAEMON: api need a Docker engine, which this executor does not provide (--no-docker); nothing was run Next: Select an executor with a Docker daemon for these targets. On Linux, the isolated steps of Node targets (npm, pnpm, Yarn) can run without Docker in a rootless crun sandbox with the same restrictions: no network, a read-only image, no capabilities and a seccomp filter. The build.isolation setting chooses: Value Meaning auto Docker when an engine answers, otherwise crun docker Always Docker crun Always crun oyzu install downloads a pinned crun, or set OYZU_CRUN to one already on the machine. If the host doesn't allow unprivileged user namespaces, the build stops with NEEDS_USER_NAMESPACES (exit 3) rather than running without the sandbox. See the daemonless sandbox.

Every language toolchain and stage tool an isolated build runs comes from oyzu.lock; the execution image supplies only the operating system, native libraries and a C toolchain. Set the tool under [tools], run oyzu pin, then build with oyzu build --isolated --full --frozen. A tool missing from the lock stops the build with the oyzu pin command that fixes it. See what runs in a container action.
documents.s: Use a pinned tool inside the container

documents.t: oyzu build --isolated --frozen --execution-images-from <bundle> uses the exact images an earlier build used. The source, Oyzu version, tool lock and targets must match, and Oyzu makes a fresh plan under your current settings. It doesn't replay old commands, and it won't substitute the current image tag for a missing image. See execution image replay.
documents.s: Reuse the images from an earlier build

documents.t: Dependencies are downloaded before actions start, from approved sources only (acquisition transport). A missing input never triggers a download during an action. Git history for version inference is fetched before the build into a private store; your checkout is never changed. Isolation doesn't prove who built something or grant permission to publish. Host builds keep your machine's capabilities: Cargo's offline mode, for example, doesn't block build scripts from the network.

Symptom Fix NEEDS_DOCKER_DAEMON (exit 3) Use a runner with Docker, or drop --isolated for builders that support the host path. NEEDS_USER_NAMESPACES (exit 3) The crun sandbox can't run here (for example kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1). Use a host that allows unprivileged user namespaces or has Docker. An image can't be found Check that Docker can reach ghcr.io and that OYZU_NO_TOOLCHAIN_PULL is unset, or build the base image locally as the execution image page shows. Oyzu never pulls an image you pass with --image; load it into Docker first. PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE A platform's executor isn't available here. The plan names the runner it needs. BUILDKIT_WORKER_UNAVAILABLE / BUILDKIT_BUILDCTL_FAILED The image worker stopped or ran out of memory. Restart it or give it more memory, then rebuild. Reference: local builds, build tasks, Docker images, target workspaces.

In a repository with several projects, build one target with what it needs, or only the targets a change affects plus the targets that use them. You need: a repository Oyzu already discovers (Adopt Oyzu), Git on PATH, and the commit you compare against available locally. The examples use two Go targets, api and worker, where worker depends on api.

Every folder a builder recognizes is one target. A native workspace (Cargo [workspace], go.work, npm, Yarn or pnpm workspaces) is one target built by its own tool; Oyzu doesn't split it into members. Relationships between targets come from what you declare: Declaration Effect depends_on: [api] in build.yaml api builds first, and a change to api also rebuilds this target. No files are passed between them. materialize.from in build.yaml This target uses another target's artifacts. Also followed by affected builds. depends_on in an oyzu.toml task Orders tasks across targets. Also followed by affected builds. Oyzu doesn't detect that one project reads another project's files. If web/ imports code from shared/, declare depends_on so a change to shared/ rebuilds web/.
# build.yaml builds: api: uses: go/app path: api worker: uses: go/app path: worker depends_on: [api] Check it with oyzu discover: each build should show Chosen by build.yaml.
documents.s: 1. Declare the targets and how they connect

documents.t: Arguments are exact target names. Targets they depend on are added automatically: $ oyzu build workerCopy … ── Selection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── requested worker required api ​ ── Plan ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 2 of 2 targets format lint test build needs api/ api skip skip skip run worker/ worker skip skip skip run api · build ​ skipped format, lint and test · fast local build profile api and worker · development · local dist only ​ ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 00:03 .. api build started 00:04 ✓ api build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o .oy… executed 1.1s 00:04 .. worker build started 00:05 ✓ worker build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o .oy… executed 1.3s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── api/ api dist/api/windows/x86_64/api-0.0.0-dev.g638adc2c9cc7.exe 2.0 MB development worker/ worker dist/worker/windows/x86_64/worker-0.0.0-dev.ge3334bd9de96.exe 2.0 MB development Checks not requested api: format-check, lint, test Checks not requested worker: format-check, lint, test ​ ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 2 executed · 6.0s api/ ✓ 1 target 1.1s worker/ ✓ 1 target 1.3s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 7212-1792552668847197300-1 Output shortened. Unrelated targets get no tools, downloads or actions, though a broken manifest elsewhere can still stop the build. An unknown name fails before anything is prepared: $ oyzu build nopeCopy … ✗ COMMAND_FAILED: unknown build target nope; available targets: api, worker Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command.
documents.s: 2. Build one target and what it needs

documents.t: --affected <git-ref> compares your working tree with a local commit. It selects every target that contains a changed file, adds the targets that depend on those (and so on), and adds the targets they need. Preview first; it runs nothing: oyzu build --affected HEAD --plan Then build. Here only api/main.go changed since HEAD: $ oyzu build --affected HEADCopy … ── Selection ───────────────────────────────────── compared with HEAD at 5259d9d changed 1 target api · 1 changed path dependents 1 target worker unaffected 0 targets not built · -v lists them ​ ── Plan ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 2 of 2 targets format lint test build why needs api/ api skip skip skip run changed worker/ worker skip skip skip run uses api api · build ​ skipped format, lint and test · fast local build profile api and worker · development · local dist only ​ ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 00:03 .. api build started 00:04 ✓ api build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o .oy… executed 1.1s 00:04 .. worker build started 00:06 ✓ worker build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o .oy… executed 1.1s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── api/ api dist/api/windows/x86_64/api-0.0.0-dev.g11bc3252f780.exe 2.0 MB development worker/ worker dist/worker/windows/x86_64/worker-0.0.0-dev.gca9a530d6b9f.exe 2.0 MB development Checks not requested api: format-check, lint, test Checks not requested worker: format-check, lint, test ​ ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 2 executed · 6.1s api/ ✓ 1 target 1.1s worker/ ✓ 1 target 1.1s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 46736-1792552676499924800-1 Output shortened. Without the depends_on line, the same change would select only api. Each selected target runs its normal checks and packaging. If nothing changed, the build writes an empty bundle and runs nothing. You can't combine --affected with target names.

In CI, compare with the branch the pull request targets. The commit must be in the local clone; Oyzu never fetches it: git fetch origin main oyzu build --affected origin/main With actions/checkout, set fetch-depth: 0 (or fetch the base branch). Blobless clones (git clone --filter=blob:none) also work. See Run in CI.

Affected builds play it safe. Oyzu builds everything, and records why, when: the base commit can't be read (the ref isn't in the local clone); a changed file belongs to no target, or a file is new since the base commit; build, configuration or lock files changed (build.yaml, oyzu.toml, oyzu.lock, or a native manifest such as go.mod); a root task with prerequisites in other targets has changed inputs, or managed configuration is active. The plan shows a full selection; the JSON record says why: $ oyzu build --affected origin/main --plan --json { "selection": { "affected": { "baselineCommit": null, "changedPaths": [], "fallback": "baseline-unavailable", "reasons": {}, "reference": "origin/main", "sourceDigest": "sha256:c88e4628600a31d68134b514eaa5230e725c4da1230e7f24efbefb219f817035" } } } A common surprise is line endings. On Windows with Git's core.autocrlf, files on disk can have CRLF endings while Git stores LF. Oyzu compares raw bytes, so every file counts as changed: $ oyzu build --affected HEAD --plan --json { "selection": { "affected": { "baselineCommit": "9a7d31fe0e4d48ba8e912063a39692e2777cf826", "changedPaths": [ "api/go.mod", "api/main.go", "api/main_test.go", "build.yaml", "worker/go.mod", "worker/main.go", "worker/main_test.go" ], "fallback": "configuration-or-lock-change", "reasons": {}, "reference": "HEAD", "sourceDigest": "sha256:d10ba07627a208004ce056654baf8d71567c7512392b3151c20dda7f382f96e5" } } } If affected builds keep selecting everything, compare changedPaths with git status, and add a .gitattributes file with explicit line endings so the working tree matches the committed bytes. Changes outside Git, such as a new tool version in your user configuration or an environment variable, aren't detected. Run a full build when those change.

In a large repository, the risk is a new project that never gets built. With a build.yaml: oyzu build --plan lists up to five folders a builder recognizes but build.yaml leaves out, under Not in build.yaml. oyzu discover --check exits 1 while such a folder exists. Run it in CI. exclude: [tools/scratch, tooling/**] marks folders that are deliberately not builds. See builds build.yaml leaves out.

For targets that declare platforms in build.yaml, oyzu build --plan --json includes a matrix you can pass to a CI matrix, one job per platform. With --affected, it holds only affected targets. See a CI matrix from the plan.

Symptom Fix Everything rebuilds every time Read selection.affected.fallback in --plan --json. Fetch the base commit, commit configuration changes, or fix line endings. A target isn't rebuilt when its dependency changes Declare the link with depends_on or materialize.from. Oyzu doesn't detect file reads across projects. unknown build target Use the names from oyzu discover. With a build.yaml, they are its build names. A folder never builds It isn't in build.yaml. Add it, or run oyzu discover --check to list such folders. Reference: affected builds, build tasks: select targets, discovery and selection.

Oyzu needs the network to download tools and dependencies the first time. After that you can build with no network at all, and when you do need the network, Oyzu can go through your company's proxy and trust its TLS-inspection certificate. You need: network access once, directly or through the proxy, to download tools and dependencies.
documents.s: Work offline or behind a proxy

documents.t: oyzu pin # pick versions and write oyzu.lock (skip if it is committed) oyzu install --frozen # install declared tools from the lock oyzu build --full # installs tools from native files and prepares dependencies, including test tools Run the same kind of build you'll need offline. --full also prepares the tools for tests, lint and format checks, which a fast build skips.

$ oyzu build --offlineCopy Building shop windows/x86_64 (host) · local · context local · fast ​ ── Prepare ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ✓ Configuration Loaded and validated <0.1s ✓ Source workspaces 2 private target workspaces ready 0.1s ✓ api dependencies Ready <0.1s ✓ worker dependencies Ready <0.1s … ✓ Tools 1 tool pinned · 0 installed now 2.9s go 1.22.12 already installed detected from go.mod … ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 00:05 .. api build started 00:09 ✓ api build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o… executed 2.8s 00:09 .. worker pre_build started 00:10 still running: worker pre_build 0s · 1 waiting 00:11 ✓ worker pre_build go vet ./... executed 2.7s 00:11 .. worker build started 00:14 ✓ worker build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o… executed 2.6s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── api/ api dist/api/windows/x86_64/api-0.0.0-dev.g638adc2c9cc7.exe 2.0 MB development worker/ worker dist/worker/windows/x86_64/worker-0.0.0-dev.ge3334bd9de96.exe 2.0 MB development Checks not requested api: format-check, lint, test Checks not requested worker: format-check, lint, test ​ ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 3 executed · 15.3s api/ ✓ 1 target 2.8s worker/ ✓ 1 target 5.4s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 32916-1792552866585130800-1 Output shortened. --offline uses only what is already on disk: it never downloads, picks new versions or writes the lock. If something is missing, the build stops and tells you what to do. Other commands take the same flag: Command Offline behavior oyzu install --frozen --offline Restores the locked tools from installed copies or cached archives; fails if an archive is missing oyzu pin --offline Resolves only from existing locks and cached metadata oyzu exec --offline -- <cmd> Uses installed tools and cached archives oyzu tools versions <tool> Needs the network unless a configured tool index has a cached copy For Rust builds on the host, cargo uses its own cache. --offline skips the fetch step and reports missing crates, but it doesn't block network access from build scripts.

Oyzu's downloads (tools, helper archives, dependencies for isolated builds, the remote cache and remote runs) use the standard proxy variables of the environment oyzu runs in: Variable Effect HTTPS_PROXY / https_proxy Proxy for HTTPS (CONNECT tunnel) HTTP_PROXY / http_proxy Proxy for HTTP ALL_PROXY / all_proxy Used when the scheme-specific variable is unset NO_PROXY / no_proxy Hosts, domains and CIDR ranges that skip the proxy SSL_CERT_FILE A PEM file of extra trusted certificates, for a TLS-inspecting proxy. The built-in public roots stay trusted Note: Proxy support is tested on Linux with HTTPS_PROXY. Windows, macOS, and real use of HTTP_PROXY and ALL_PROXY are not supported yet.

export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.example:3128 export NO_PROXY=.corp.example,10.0.0.0/8 export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/corp/inspection-ca.pem # only if the proxy inspects TLS In PowerShell, use $env:HTTPS_PROXY = '…'. You can put credentials in the proxy URL (http://user:password@proxy:3128); Oyzu never prints them.

Run something that only needs the network: oyzu tools versions go oyzu install --dry-run go@1.27 A wrong setting fails right away. Oyzu never falls back to a direct connection: $ HTTPS_PROXY='not a url' oyzu tools versions goCopy ✗ PROXY_INVALID: HTTPS_PROXY is not a valid proxy URL Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command. $ SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/missing.pem oyzu tools versions goCopy ✗ TRUST_BUNDLE_UNREADABLE: SSL_CERT_FILE cannot be read: The system cannot find the file specified. (os error 2) Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command. An empty or malformed certificate file fails with TRUST_BUNDLE_INVALID.

Local addresses skip the proxy: localhost, 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1. A proxy doesn't widen what Oyzu downloads. Oyzu still only contacts the approved sources for each tool or dependency. A TLS-inspecting proxy can read request headers, including any credentials sent to a source. Only use a proxy you trust with them. Native tools use their own settings. Cargo, npm, Maven and other tools that download for themselves on the host path use their own proxy and certificate configuration. Not supported: proxy authentication other than credentials in the URL, PAC files, the operating system's proxy settings, and different proxies per source.

An administrator can send Node tool downloads through an internal mirror with the administrative registries.routes setting and a connector binding file passed with oyzu install --connector-bindings <file>. The mirror must serve the standard Node distribution layout, and credentials come from an environment variable named in the binding. If the binding is missing or a request is denied, Oyzu doesn't fall back to the public source. Supported on Linux. See tool proxy acquisition.

Message Cause and fix Preparation fails under --offline, naming a tool or dependency It was never downloaded. Go online once and run the same build (with --full if you need checks). TOOL_LOCK_MISSING There is no lock to restore from. Run oyzu pin or oyzu install online. TOOL_OFFLINE tools versions needs the network for this tool. PROXY_INVALID Fix the proxy URL (scheme, host, numeric port). TRUST_BUNDLE_UNREADABLE / TRUST_BUNDLE_INVALID Point SSL_CERT_FILE at a readable, non-empty PEM file. SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE The download failed after retries (408, 429, 502, 503, 504 and connection errors are retried twice). Check the proxy and your connection. SOURCE_TIMEOUT The 45-second download deadline passed. SOURCE_DENIED (403) No approved source allows that request or redirect. This is a source setting, not a proxy problem. Reference: acquisition transport, tool commands.
What each part of the build output means, how to show more or less of it, how to use it from scripts, and how to look up a build days later. You need: a project you have built at least once.

A build prints the same sections in the same order in a terminal and in a CI log: Section What it tells you Title line Project, platform, local or CI, the build context (local, pr, ci, release), and fast or full Prepare Each preparation step with its result and time: configuration, tool versions and installs, workspaces, dependencies, output bundle. The Tools row lists each tool and why it is there Selection Only when the build was narrowed (--affected or named targets): what was requested, changed, needed or left out Plan Targets by stage, marked run, skip or -, with a note per skip reason and needs for order between targets Build One row per action: elapsed time, mark, target, stage, the native command, executed or reused, and duration Failure / Warnings One section each, with the cause, exit code, log file and the narrowest re-run command Outputs Each artifact with its path and size Summary Tests run now (or reused test evidence), coverage, the result line, and Details: the manifest, event log and invocation ID Each row starts with a mark: ✓ succeeded, ↺ reused, ! warning, ✗ failed, .. started, ⊘ blocked. Without color the marks are paired with words, so the meaning never depends on color. A reused row shows how long the original run took (was 1.3s), and reused tests are reported as Reused test evidence … not run now. The tutorial shows a full failure section.
documents.s: 1. Read a build top to bottom

documents.t: Flag or variable Effect -q Hide routine progress; keep results, warnings, errors and native tool output -v / -vv Debug / trace detail, such as per-target cache details and every unaffected target --log-level <level> Set the threshold: error, warn, info (default), debug, trace OYZU_LOG=warn,oyzu::executor=trace Per-area levels from the environment; any command-line flag overrides it --output interactive Use the live dashboard; the default auto prints line by line NO_COLOR=1 Plain text. Color is also off when output is redirected None of these change what is built, cached or checked.

Every command takes --json, before or after the subcommand: oyzu --json build oyzu build --plan --json oyzu --json history Standard output then holds exactly one JSON result; diagnostics go to standard error as JSON Lines. Errors are JSON too: $ oyzu --json build nope { "code": "COMMAND_FAILED", "error": "unknown build target nope; available targets: api, worker", "evidence": { "manifest": ".\\dist/manifest.json", "note": "Verify its invocation identity; it may describe an earlier operation", "status": "available" }, "exitCode": 1, "invocationId": "38300-1792552823921616500-1", "nextStep": "Correct the reported cause and retry the command." } Parse the JSON, not the human output. Each command has its own JSON shape and may gain fields, so ignore fields you don't recognize.

Each build replaces dist/ and moves the previous bundle to .oyzu/history/. oyzu history lists the kept builds, newest first: $ oyzu historyCopy Invocation evidence Invocation / run Outcome Scope Started 32916-1792552866585130800-1 succeeded 2 targets · 3 actions 2026-10-21T03:21:12.476057400+00:00 16232-1792552806550250500-1 succeeded 2 targets · 9 actions 2026-10-21T03:20:12.159576900+00:00 57240-1792552779758664800-1 succeeded 2 targets · 2 actions 2026-10-21T03:19:43.009968100+00:00 … The list shows up to twenty builds. It only reads local files; it doesn't use the network or run anything.

Pass the invocation ID from a build's Details line (a run ID also works): $ oyzu history 32916-1792552866585130800-1Copy Invocation evidence Outcome: succeeded Invocation: 32916-1792552866585130800-1 Run: 32916-1792552872476057400 Scope: 2 targets · 3 actions ​ Actions Executed: 3 Checks not requested api: format-check, lint, test Checks not requested worker: format-check, lint, test ​ Why each stage ran or was reused api:build — Executed Recorded selection: api (selected) Reuse: action definition changed: api:build env.GOPROXY added, api:build extensions, api:format-check argv removed and 61 more Source detail unavailable: file-level membership of the effective target scope is unavailable worker:pre_build — Executed Recorded selection: worker (selected) Reuse: contains authored tasks or hooks without declared outputs, which are never cached by default Source detail unavailable: file-level comparison evidence was not recorded worker:build — Executed Recorded selection: worker (selected) Reuse: contains authored tasks or hooks without declared outputs, which are never cached by default Source detail unavailable: file-level comparison evidence was not recorded manifest: …\shop\dist\manifest.json bundle: …\shop\dist events: …\shop\dist\logs\events.jsonl plan: …\shop\dist\plan.json 0 more diagnostics · 0 more failures omitted Next: oyzu inspect <bundle-directory> --json for full verified records Recorded observations; this summary does not verify artifact contents. The summary shows at most eight decisions, failures and diagnostics, and never native log contents or environment values. The full record is in the files it lists.

oyzu inspect # this project's bundle (dist/ by default) oyzu inspect .oyzu/history/<run-id> # an earlier build If your project already uses dist/ for its own output, set [build] bundleDirectory = ".oyzu/bundle" in the root oyzu.toml. oyzu inspect and oyzu history then use that folder. See bundle destination. $ oyzu inspectCopy ✓ Bundle contents verified · build succeeded Run 32916-1792552872476057400 · source sha256:d48c2ec36d6c · uncommitted changes ​ Targets Target Builder Platform Path api go/app windows/x86_64 api worker go/app windows/x86_64 worker ​ Actions Action Status Exit Gate api:build succeeded 0 required worker:pre_build succeeded 0 required worker:build succeeded 0 required ​ Artifacts Path (under dist/) Kind Size Platform Digest api/windows/x86_64/ file 2.0 MB windows/x86_64 sha256:32838a192b1b api-0.0.0-dev.g638adc2c9cc7.exe worker/windows/x86_64/ file 2.0 MB windows/x86_64 sha256:413317212b94 worker-0.0.0-dev.ge3334bd9de96.exe ​ Verified: every recorded file matches its digest. This does not show who produced the build or that it may be released. Use --json for the full manifest, including the plan and execution envelope. inspect checks every recorded file against its digest, the test reports against the build's rules, and the manifest against the plan. It doesn't tell you who built the bundle or whether it may be released. uncommitted changes means the source had local edits.

Path Contents manifest.json What was built: targets, actions with results and exit codes, artifacts with digests, reuse, selection, context plan.json The plan the build followed envelope.json Run details, including the start time and invocation ID logs/events.jsonl The event log. Other files in logs/ hold each action's native output Per-target folders Artifacts and reports/ (JUnit, coverage) A failed build still writes a bundle; read manifest.json for what actually happened. Full layout: build bundles.

Symptom Fix INVOCATION_NOT_FOUND The ID isn't in dist/ or .oyzu/history/. Run oyzu history for the kept IDs. Only recent builds are kept, so a missing entry doesn't mean a build succeeded. INVOCATION_ID_INVALID Copy the ID exactly from the Details line or the list. inspect reports a mismatch A file in the bundle changed after the build. Rebuild, and don't ship from that bundle. An error names a .oyzu/bundle-… folder The build kept its results there because it couldn't finish writing dist/. Inspect that folder, fix the disk or permission problem, then rebuild. No color in a terminal NO_COLOR is set, or output is redirected. CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 forces color. Reference: CLI output, build logging, build bundles: retained invocation lookup. Concept: build evidence.

Build an existing repository with Oyzu without changing how it builds today. Start with no Oyzu files, check what Oyzu detects, and add configuration only where it can't decide on its own. You need: oyzu on your PATH (Install Oyzu), a Git checkout of your project, and network access for the first build so Oyzu can download the tools your project asks for. The examples use a repository called shop with two Go modules, api/ and worker/.
documents.s: Adopt Oyzu in an existing repository

documents.t: From the repository root, with no Oyzu files: $ oyzu discoverCopy 2 targets · 12 tasks discovered without running project code Project root: …\shop ​ project-api · go/app Chosen by detected from project files Location api Manager go Version 0.0.0 Part of builds build, format-check, lint, test Development tasks format, install ​ project-worker · go/app Chosen by detected from project files Location worker Manager go Version 0.0.0 Part of builds build, format-check, lint, test Development tasks format, install ​ Target names are what `oyzu build <target>` accepts. Next steps: oyzu run list every task and the command it runs oyzu build --plan preview the build stages without running them Use --json for the complete discovery record, including each task's environment and dependencies. Oyzu reads native files only (here, each go.mod); it runs nothing. Each folder a builder recognizes becomes a target, named project at the root and project-<path> below it. Discovery stops at the first folder a builder recognizes, so a native workspace (Cargo workspace, go.work, npm or pnpm workspace) is one target built by its own tool. Nested Git repositories and folders with their own build.yaml are skipped.

$ oyzu run listCopy Available tasks · 12 across 2 targets ​ Task Source Command project-api · go/app (6) project-api:build Inferred · go go build ./... project-api:format Inferred · go gofmt -w . project-api:format-check Inferred · go gofmt -l . project-api:install Inferred · go go mod download project-api:lint Inferred · go go vet ./... project-api:test Inferred · go go test ./... … If something is wrong (a missing target, the wrong package manager or test runner), fix it in step 6.

oyzu build --plan # preview only: installs, downloads and runs nothing oyzu build # fast local build: build and package stages, plus required checks oyzu build --full # also runs tests, lint and format checks The first oyzu build installs the tool versions your native files ask for and builds every target: $ oyzu buildCopy Building shop windows/x86_64 (host) · local · context local · fast ​ ── Prepare ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ✓ Configuration Loaded and validated <0.1s ✓ Tool versions Resolved and locked 6.1s ✓ Source workspaces 2 private target workspaces ready <0.1s ✓ project-api dependencies Ready <0.1s ✓ project-worker dependencies Ready <0.1s ✓ Output bundle Ready <0.1s ✓ Compiler cache 0.0 MiB / 8192 MiB retained budget <0.1s ✓ Compiler cache 0.0 MiB / 8192 MiB retained budget <0.1s ✓ Source evidence 8 captured/observed entries recorded in 0.00s <0.1s ✓ CLI identity Verified in 0.05s <0.1s ✓ Report preparation Contracts and bindings ready <0.1s ✓ Tools 1 tool pinned · 0 installed now 0.3s go 1.22.12 already installed detected from go.mod ​ … ── Plan ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 2 targets format lint test build api/ project-api skip skip skip run worker/ project-worker skip skip skip run ​ skipped format, lint and test · fast local build profile project-api and project-worker · development · local dist only ​ ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 00:07 .. project-api build started 00:07 .. project-worker build started 00:10 still running: project-api build 2s · project-worker build 2s 00:11 ✓ project-api build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=fals… executed 3.2s 00:11 ✓ project-worker build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=fals… executed 3.1s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── api/ project-api 2.0 MB development dist/project-api/windows/x86_64/project-api-0.0.0-dev.g638adc2c9cc7.exe worker/ project-worker 2.0 MB development dist/project-worker/windows/x86_64/project-worker-0.0.0-dev.gfae7445fa954.exe Checks not requested project-api: format-check, lint, test Checks not requested project-worker: format-check, lint, test ​ ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 2 executed · 11.4s api/ ✓ 1 target 3.2s worker/ ✓ 1 target 3.1s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 58632-1792552643943202500-1 Output shortened. A local build skips tests, lint and format checks unless a check is required. In CI or with --full, every check that isn't off runs. See Run in CI.

The first build writes these into the project root: Path What to do Why oyzu.lock Commit it It records exact tool versions and digests, so everyone and CI get the same tools .oyzu-tool-lock-edit.lock Ignore it A coordination file for concurrent lock writes; it holds no data dist/ Ignore it The output bundle of the latest build .oyzu/ Ignore it Local state: build history, compiler state, .oyzu/bin outputs # .gitignore dist/ .oyzu/ .oyzu-tool-lock-edit.lock If you commit the coordination file, builds warn SOURCE_TRACKED_IGNORED. Untrack it with git rm --cached .oyzu-tool-lock-edit.lock.
documents.s: 4. Commit the lock, ignore the outputs

documents.t: Most repositories need nothing more. When you do need configuration, each setting has exactly one home: Ask File Examples Does your ecosystem's own file already say it? The native file The go line in go.mod, rust-toolchain.toml, packageManager in package.json, global.json, Gradle and Maven wrapper properties Does it change what is built or how builds connect: which builds exist, their names, builder, platforms, dependencies, builder options? build.yaml at the root builds:, uses, path, platforms, depends_on, inputs, with Could it differ by folder, context (local, PR, CI, release) or person, or need an organization-wide limit? oyzu.toml (and oyzu.local.toml for personal values) [tools], [checks], [tasks], [build.executors], [publish] Write each tool version once, and never in build.yaml. If rust-toolchain.toml pins Rust, don't repeat it in oyzu.toml. A native minimum (Go's go line, Cargo's rust-version) is a constraint that [tools] can satisfy with an exact version.
documents.s: 5. Decide which file a setting belongs in

documents.t: Add a build.yaml at the root to name builds, connect them, limit platforms, exclude folders, or make a choice discovery won't guess. With a build.yaml, only the builds it lists exist. builds: api: uses: go/app path: api worker: uses: go/app path: worker depends_on: [api] # build api first; rebuild worker when api changes Run oyzu discover again: each build now shows Chosen by build.yaml. Each build accepts these fields: uses, path, platforms, depends_on, inputs, materialize, bindings, fetches and with. Any other field fails with CONFIG_INVALID_VALUE naming it. The root keys are builds and exclude. The full format is in configuration: build inventory. Good to know: uses is optional when only one builder recognizes the folder: web: {path: web} is complete. Renaming changes identity. New names change output paths and cache keys, so those targets rebuild once. Let Oyzu write it. oyzu discover --write adds every folder exactly one builder recognizes, keeping the default names. oyzu discover --check exits 1 while a build is neither listed nor excluded; run it in CI. See builds build.yaml leaves out. Ambiguous choices fail with a fix. When native files point two ways (for example both black and ruff configured in pyproject.toml), discovery stops and names the setting to add under with: ✗ COMMAND_FAILED: conflicting Python formatter candidates black, ruff: black via pyproject.toml tool.black; ruff via pyproject.toml tool.ruff; declare the intended one for this target in build.yaml with `with: {formatter: black}` or `with: {formatter: ruff}` The settings each builder accepts are listed in selecting a role in build.yaml.

oyzu.toml files apply from the root down to each target folder, and the nearer file wins: # oyzu.toml at the root [tools] go = "1.27" # exact team version; satisfies go.mod's minimum [checks] lint = "advisory" # lint failures warn instead of failing the build [context.release.checks] tests = "required" # release builds always run tests Check it after every edit: $ oyzu config validateCopy Configuration ​ Capabilities: • config.cascade/v1 • config.profiles/v1 • config.removal/v1 • config.env-path/v1 • policy.constraints/v1 Diagnostics: (none) Valid: yes oyzu config show, get <key> and explain <key> show resolved values and where they came from. Personal values go in oyzu.local.toml, which you don't commit.

oyzu discover # every target you expect, with the right builder oyzu build --plan # the stages and tool versions you expect oyzu build --full # builds, tests, lints and format-checks everything Then commit oyzu.lock, any build.yaml and oyzu.toml, and your .gitignore changes.

Symptom Cause and fix A folder is missing from oyzu discover It's inside another target or a nested Git repository, or no builder recognizes it. Add it to build.yaml with uses and path. A folder is missing after you added build.yaml With a root build.yaml, only listed builds exist. Add the entry, or run oyzu discover --write. CONFIG_INVALID_VALUE naming an unknown field or root key build.yaml accepts only the fields listed above, and builds must be under builds:. CONFIG_INVALID_VALUE for a folder several builders recognize Name the builder: both: {uses: docker/image, path: both}. conflicting … candidates Add the with: setting the message names. Another tool's build.yaml (for example Dart's) Oyzu only treats a file with a builds, members or exclude root key as its own. Others are listed as skipped. More symptoms: Troubleshooting. Reference: discovery and selection, configuration, build tasks. Next: Monorepos and affected builds · Pin tools for your team · Run tasks

oyzu publish takes the artifacts a build already produced and uploads exactly those bytes to an OCI registry or an existing GitHub release, with their provenance attached. It reads every upload back before reporting success. You don't need an account. Oyzu's own Preview releases are binary-only, from oyzuai/oyzu-releases: the release audit checks the binaries, notices and source before publishing, and recipients use oyzu --licenses offline or download the platform's oyzu-notices-<os>-<arch>.txt from the same release. Note: Publishing is experimental. OCI publishing is supported on Linux and GitHub release publishing on Windows x64; authenticated registries and GitHub Enterprise are not supported yet. npm, PyPI, OCI image archives and mutable OCI tags are not available, and kind = "npm" or "pypi" fails configuration validation. You need: A successful build bundle (dist/manifest.json). A signed provenance bundle for each artifact, produced by your own signing step before you publish: a Sigstore v0.3 bundle with one DSSE envelope carrying in-toto SLSA build provenance, signed with an Ed25519 key you control. Oyzu checks it; it doesn't create it. An Ed25519 publication signing seed in an environment variable. Oyzu signs a record of what it is about to publish with it. Destination credentials in environment variables. Network access. Publishing doesn't work offline.

[publish] is only accepted in the project root's oyzu.toml or oyzu.local.toml; anywhere else it fails with CONFIG_SCOPE. Never write secrets here, only the names of the environment variables that hold them. [publish] default = "registry" [publish.destinations.registry] kind = "oci" registry = "https://registry.example.com" repository = "team/artifacts" artifacts = ["api"] # output IDs; optional when the bundle has one artifact usernameEnv = "REGISTRY_USERNAME" passwordEnv = "REGISTRY_PASSWORD" [publish.destinations.github] kind = "github-release" apiUrl = "https://api.github.com" repository = "your-org/your-repo" tokenEnv = "GITHUB_RELEASE_TOKEN" artifacts = ["api", "worker"] [publish.destinations.github.evidence] mode = "destination" [publish.sets] release = ["registry", "github"] [publish.requirements.provenance] bundlePath = "evidence/build.sigstore.json" publicKey = "<base64 raw 32-byte Ed25519 builder public key>" builderId = "https://ci.example.com/builders/release" [publish.requirements.signing] keyEnv = "PUBLICATION_SIGNING_SEED" publicKey = "<base64 raw 32-byte Ed25519 publication public key>" Replace the values in angle brackets and the example hosts with your own keys and endpoints. Choosing artifacts. Each artifacts entry is an output ID: the target name for its main output (api), target/name for another output (app/archive), and optionally a platform (cli/bin-oyzu@linux/x86_64). oyzu config validate, oyzu build --plan and every build reject unknown names, so a typo shows up long before release day. Different provenance per artifact. Use [publish.requirements.provenance.byArtifact."<output-id>"] entries instead of the single form. {artifact.platform} in bundlePath picks one bundle per platform. See publishing finalized artifacts. Check the configuration: oyzu config validate
documents.s: 1. Configure destinations in the root oyzu.toml

documents.t: oyzu build --full oyzu inspect oyzu publish --destination registry Without --destination, Oyzu uses publish.default. Repeat --destination, or name a set (--destination release), to publish to several places. Before uploading, Oyzu checks the selection, verifies each provenance bundle against your public key and builder ID, and signs the publication record. It reports success only after reading every object back by digest. With no configuration, you get: $ oyzu publishCopy Publishing the build Verifying publication requirements and destination results ✗ PUBLISH_NOT_CONFIGURED: configure publish.destinations in oyzu.toml Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command.

The published reference is registry/repository@sha256:<manifest-digest>; tags are not used. The OCI artifact holds your file plus the provenance and publication record as separate layers. Publishing identical content again reports already-present. HTTPS is required (plain HTTP only for registries on localhost), and the registry's bearer-token challenge is supported.

Oyzu attaches assets to a release that already exists, at an existing tag. It never creates tags or releases, changes release details or deletes assets. The token needs Contents read/write on the repository. The release is chosen like this: --tag <tag>, if given (for example in a manually started release job). Otherwise, the exact version tag the build recorded for the built commit (v1.4.0, or api/v1.4.2 for one package in a workspace). If the build recorded no tag, publishing stops with PUBLISH_TAG_UNKNOWN before contacting the network. Tag the commit, rebuild and publish again, or pass --tag. Asset names include the platform (oyzu built for linux/x86_64 becomes oyzu-linux-x86_64), so one release can hold every platform.

Build each platform in its own job, collect the bundles, and publish once: oyzu publish --destination github \ --manifest bundles/linux-x86_64/dist/manifest.json \ --manifest bundles/darwin-arm64/dist/manifest.json For targets that declare platforms in build.yaml, publishing in the release context without every declared platform fails with PUBLISH_PLATFORMS_INCOMPLETE, naming each missing one. To publish anyway, name each missing platform with a reason; the reason is recorded in the signed publication record: oyzu publish --destination github --allow-incomplete windows/arm64="runner not available"
documents.s: 3. Publish several platforms as one release

documents.t: The output shows each destination's result with the reference and digest read back. oyzu --json publish … returns operationId, status, planDigest, artifacts and destinations; each destination is published, already-present, failed or unfinished. Exit Meaning 0 Every selected destination was published, or already had the content 1 Refused before publishing: missing provenance, wrong subject, invalid selection, or a conflicting existing asset 2 At least one destination failed or is unfinished. Destinations that succeeded stay published. Fix the cause and run the same command again; finished destinations are matched by digest

Code Fix PUBLISH_NOT_CONFIGURED Add [publish.destinations.*] to the root oyzu.toml. CONFIG_SCOPE [publish] is in a subfolder's oyzu.toml. Move it to the root. PUBLISH_ARTIFACT_SELECTION_INVALID An output ID is unknown or ambiguous, or the bundle has several artifacts and none is selected. Use the IDs from the build's Outputs. PUBLISH_EVIDENCE_MISSING A selected artifact (or platform) has no provenance bundle. Produce it, or add a byArtifact entry. PUBLISH_TAG_UNKNOWN, PUBLISH_TAG_CONFLICT, PUBLISH_TAG_COMMIT_MISMATCH Oyzu can't tell which release tag to use. Tag the built commit and rebuild, or pass --tag. PUBLISH_PLATFORMS_INCOMPLETE A declared platform has no artifact. Add its bundle with another --manifest, or use --allow-incomplete <platform>=<reason>. PUBLISH_BINDING_UNPUSHED A Helm chart that refers to an image is being published without that image. Add the image's destination to the same publish. PUBLISH_VERIFICATION_MISSING Policy requires a verification run the bundles don't include. Pass that bundle with --manifest. Reference: publishing finalized artifacts, release check, version inference.

--remote runs oyzu build or oyzu run <task> on a platform pool instead of your machine, against the exact commit you pushed, and streams the output back to your terminal. It is the only part of Oyzu that needs a platform account; everything else works without one. Note: Remote builds are experimental. The client is supported on Linux. You need: A Git checkout whose HEAD is pushed to a github.com repository linked to a project in your platform account, and git on PATH. The platform URL and your account name in your user (or machine, or administrative) configuration. Project files can't set them, so a checkout can't redirect your credentials. A platform credential: a token in OYZU_PLATFORM_TOKEN (read from the environment, never stored), or a session from oyzu auth login (experimental).

This runs locally and contacts nothing: $ oyzu build --remote --planCopy Planning shop All declared platforms · Remote pool · context local · Full checks requested ​ Build preview Execution: remote · No tools installed, dependencies downloaded or build actions run. ​ api · go/app · unresolved until executor selection Executor: captured-worker Profile: development · local dist only (no difference: the Go compiler always optimizes) Placement: runs on any platform · Docker engine required · Isolated steps run in the captured worker on a Docker engine Stage Selection Details build selected Native commands and report bindings resolve during preparation format-check selected Native commands and report bindings resolve during preparation lint selected Native commands and report bindings resolve during preparation test selected Native commands and report bindings resolve during preparation prepare unresolved Target environment setup is determined by native dependency preparation package unresolved Artifact packaging is determined by native metadata ​ … Output shortened. A pool always runs full checks in isolation, so every check is selected, and the plan shows what each target needs from the pool.
documents.s: 1. Preview what the pool would run

documents.t: oyzu config set --global platform.url https://platform.example.com oyzu config set --global platform.account payments export OYZU_PLATFORM_TOKEN=… # or: oyzu auth login In CI, set OYZU_PLATFORM_URL, OYZU_PLATFORM_ACCOUNT and OYZU_PLATFORM_TOKEN in the environment instead. Without configuration, --remote stops before sending anything: $ oyzu build --remoteCopy Building shop remotely Platform pool · pushed HEAD · full checks, isolated · Ctrl-C cancels the run ✗ REMOTE_NOT_CONFIGURED: set platform.url to the platform URL, for example `oyzu config set --global platform.url https://platform.example.com` Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command.

Command What runs remotely oyzu build --remote Every target oyzu build cli web --remote Targets cli and web and what they depend on oyzu build --affected origin/main --remote Targets affected since the merge base of origin/main and HEAD oyzu run policy-check --remote One task (target:task also works) … --remote --download out Any of the above, then downloads every output into out/ Push first: the pool checks out the pushed commit, so uncommitted changes are not included (you get a warning). Output streams back in the same layout as a local build, with each line labelled by target or task. It ends with a receipt: result, run ID, commit, project, Oyzu version and the outputs produced. Nothing is written locally unless you pass --download. The first Ctrl-C asks the platform to cancel and keeps following the run until the pool confirms. A second Ctrl-C exits immediately. Closing the terminal doesn't cancel the run.

Remote result Exit Succeeded 0 Oyzu exited non-zero on the pool That exit code Failed before Oyzu ran, skipped, cancelled, timed out or unknown 1 Refused before or while creating the run 2 Interrupted with Ctrl-C 130 If the client loses track of a run after creating it, the result is unknown, not failed: it exits 1 with the last state it saw and never starts local work instead. Check the run with the link it printed before starting another.

A refused remote run never falls back to a local build. Code Fix REMOTE_NOT_CONFIGURED Set platform.url and platform.account in user configuration. REMOTE_UNAUTHENTICATED Set a current OYZU_PLATFORM_TOKEN, or sign in with oyzu auth login. Unattended runs never use a person's session. REMOTE_COMMIT_NOT_PUSHED HEAD isn't on any branch of the remote. Push it. REMOTE_COMMIT_NOT_FOUND The platform can't see the commit yet. Push and retry. REMOTE_REPOSITORY_NOT_LINKED Link the repository to a project in your platform account. REMOTE_REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED Only github.com repositories are supported. REMOTE_NOT_A_CHECKOUT Run from a Git checkout.

You can't pass task arguments after -- to a remote run. There is no --detach, and you can't list runs or re-attach to one from the CLI. Retries honor Retry-After and reuse the same request key, so a retry never starts a second run. The client works through HTTPS_PROXY and needs only outbound access. Reference: remote runs, planning a remote run, authentication.

oyzu run runs your project's everyday commands (test, lint, format, your own scripts) with the project's pinned tools, the same way in every repository. You need: a project Oyzu discovers. Tools a task needs are installed from oyzu.lock the first time. The examples use a repository with two Go targets, api and worker.

$ oyzu run listCopy Available tasks · 13 across 2 targets ​ Task Source Command api · go/app (7) api:build Inferred · go go build ./... api:format Inferred · go gofmt -w . api:format-check Inferred · go gofmt -l . api:install Inferred · go go mod download api:lint Inferred · go go vet ./... api:smoke oyzu.toml go run . api:test Inferred · go go test ./... ​ worker · go/app (6) worker:build Inferred · go go build ./... worker:format Inferred · go gofmt -w . worker:format-check Inferred · go gofmt -l . worker:install Inferred · go go mod download worker:lint Inferred · go go vet ./... worker:test Inferred · go go test ./... ​ Run one with: oyzu run <task> (extra arguments go after --) Commands show argv; task dependencies and hooks may also run. Use --json for full task records. Tasks come from two places, shown in the Source column: Inferred: the builder reads native files (go.mod, Cargo.toml, package.json scripts and so on). oyzu.toml: tasks you add yourself. There is no fixed task list for every project, so start from what oyzu run list shows.

In a project with one target, the bare name works: oyzu run test. With several targets, add the target name: $ oyzu run api:testCopy · Setup Loading configuration and discovering tasks · Skipped api · Compiling · Not included in the selected action graph · Skipped api · Checking formatting, api · Linting · fast local build · Actions 1 known; counts do not estimate time remaining › Build Running selected work › api · Testing Running {"Time":"2026-10-20T23:18:57.3274085-04:00","Action":"start","Package":"example.com/shop/api"} … {"Time":"2026-10-20T23:18:57.5269071-04:00","Action":"pass","Package":"example.com/shop/api","Elapsed":0.199} · api · Testing TEST_EVIDENCE: Test evidence api:test Command passed Results 1 passed · 0 failed · 0 skipped Coverage 50.0% of statements (1/2) Acceptance accepted ✓ api · Testing Succeeded (exit 0 after 2.24s) The native tool's own output appears unchanged (here, go test -json), with a few lines from Oyzu around it. If several targets define the same task, an unqualified name is refused rather than guessed: $ oyzu run testCopy · Setup Loading configuration and discovering tasks ✗ COMMAND_FAILED: ambiguous task test; choose api:test, worker:test Next: Correct the reported cause and retry the command. To run from another folder, use -C: oyzu -C services/api run test.
Everything after -- goes to the task's command: oyzu run api:test -- -run TestGreeting
documents.s: 3. Pass arguments to the native command

documents.t: Add a table under [tasks] in oyzu.toml. The command is an argv list and never goes through a shell. # oyzu.toml at the repository root [tasks."api:smoke"] # belongs to build api, runs in api/ argv = ["go", "run", "."] $ oyzu run api:smokeCopy · Setup Loading configuration and discovering tasks › api:smoke Running · native tool output follows Hello, Oyzu! ✓ api:smoke Succeeded (exit 0 after 1.16s) A task runs with its build's tools, environment and folder. cwd changes the folder, relative to the file that declares the task. Adding a task never installs a new tool: a task that runs node needs a target whose tools include Node. Where a task applies depends on its key and file: Key Applies to [tasks."api:smoke"] Build api only [tasks.lint-docs] in the root oyzu.toml The whole repository: oyzu run lint-docs [tasks.lint-docs] in a subfolder's oyzu.toml Every build below that folder [tasks.test] (a stage name) Replaces that stage in every build the file reaches. Qualify it when those builds use different builders A misspelled build name, or a task key in a file outside its build's folder, is an error naming the file and line.

A task named pre_<stage> or post_<stage> runs before or after that stage in oyzu build: [tasks."worker:pre_build"] argv = ["go", "vet", "./..."] $ oyzu buildCopy … ── Build ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── 00:03 .. api build started 00:04 ✓ api build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o… executed 1.2s 00:04 .. worker pre_build started 00:05 ✓ worker pre_build go vet ./... executed 1.2s 00:05 .. worker build started 00:07 ✓ worker build go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -o… executed 1.1s ​ ── Outputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── api/ api dist/api/windows/x86_64/api-0.0.0-dev.g638adc2c9cc7.exe 2.0 MB development worker/ worker dist/worker/windows/x86_64/worker-0.0.0-dev.ge3334bd9de96.exe 2.0 MB development Checks not requested api: format-check, lint, test Checks not requested worker: format-check, lint, test ​ ✓ Build succeeded 2 targets · 3 executed · 7.3s api/ ✓ 1 target 1.2s worker/ ✓ 1 target 2.3s Details dist/manifest.json · dist/logs/events.jsonl · invocation 58428-1792552742079235600-1 Output shortened. Tasks and hooks can depend on other tasks with depends_on = ["schema:verify"]. A prerequisite runs once per command, even when several tasks need it. Two things to know: Hooks run on every build. A hook without declared outputs means its target can't be reused from the cache, because Oyzu can't see what the hook changed. oyzu history <id> says so: contains authored tasks or hooks without declared outputs, which are never cached by default. See Cache build results. Conditions choose when a hook runs; they don't make it mandatory. when and unless limit a hook to certain contexts, platforms, profiles or artifacts: [tasks."cli:post_build"] argv = ["{artifact.path}", "--version"] # smoke-test each built binary when = { optimized = true, platform = ["linux/x86_64"] } For checks that must run, use check levels instead.

oyzu --json run list # the task list as JSON oyzu --json run api:test # a structured result; the exit status is kept When a task fails, oyzu run exits with the task's own exit code. Tasks run with oyzu run run on your machine and are never cached; use oyzu build for cached, recorded results. oyzu run <task> --remote runs a task on a platform pool (Remote builds).

Message Fix ambiguous task test; choose api:test, worker:test Add the target name to the task. TASK_NOT_FOUND: no task "nope" … (exit 5) Check oyzu run list and the folder you're in; use oyzu -C <project> run <task>. CONFIG_REFERENCE_UNKNOWN A task key names a build or hook target that doesn't exist. The message suggests the nearest name. CONFIG_TASK_AMBIGUOUS An unqualified stage replacement reaches builds with different builders. Qualify it per build. A format task is refused in a build Tasks that change files, such as format, are for oyzu run only. Builds use the read-only format-check. Reference: build tasks (hooks, conditions, placeholders), CLI output.

Set up a project so every developer and CI job uses the same compiler, runtime and package-manager versions, with nothing installed by hand. You need: a project Oyzu discovers and network access for the first download. No account. Note: Tool management is fully tested on Linux x86-64; Windows x86-64 works with less test coverage, and macOS isn't supported yet. Automatic installation isn't available for every tool on every platform.

File Holds Who edits it Native pin files What your ecosystem already says: rust-toolchain.toml, go.mod (the go line is a minimum), global.json, packageManager in package.json, Gradle and Maven wrapper properties You, as today oyzu.toml [tools] What a native file can't say, such as an exact Go version or a tool no native file names oyzu install, oyzu uninstall, or you oyzu.lock The exact version, download and digest of every tool, for every platform your team uses Only Oyzu (pin, install, update) Commit all three. Write each version in one place: if a native file pins it, leave it out of oyzu.toml.

$ oyzu pin --dry-runCopy Build requirements · preview ​ Consolidated across 2 build target(s). ​ Tool requirements Requirement Requested version Needed for Installation support Applies to oyzu:go 1.22 Declared requirement Oyzu All targets ​ Executor prerequisites Requirement Needed for Availability Applies to ​ Check tools are required when their checks are enabled by the build or policy. ​ Tool execution platform coverage OS Architecture ABI darwin arm64 native linux amd64 gnu linux arm64 gnu windows amd64 msvc Metadata coverage only; native installation support varies. ​ No files changed. Tool resolution complete. Installed availability was not checked. Nothing was installed. Use --json for sources, constraints and discovery limitations. --dry-run writes and installs nothing. Add --json to see each requirement's source and constraint.

If your native files already say everything (for example rust-toolchain.toml with an exact version), you only need a lock: oyzu pin # pick exact versions and write oyzu.lock; installs nothing The first oyzu build writes a lock if there isn't one.
