Add the schema line at the top of the file and an editor with Taplo (for example VS Code's Even Better TOML) completes keys and flags wrong values: #:schema https://github.com/oyzuai/oyzu-releases/releases/latest/download/oyzu.toml.schema.json oyzu config schema oyzu.toml prints the same schema offline. The CLI's own checks stay authoritative; see editor schemas.

Command Does oyzu config validate [--strict] [--all-profiles] Checks every file; --strict also fails on warnings. oyzu config get <key> Prints the effective value. oyzu config explain <key> Shows the value, every source that set it, and why it won. oyzu config show Prints the whole effective configuration. oyzu config set <key> <value> (--project | --local | --global) Writes a value to the project oyzu.toml, its oyzu.local.toml or the user file; exactly one is required. Add --profile NAME to write inside that profile. oyzu config unset <key> (--project | --local | --global) Removes it from that file, exposing inherited values. oyzu config profiles Lists profiles and which is selected. oyzu config schema oyzu.toml Prints the JSON Schema. None of them run project tasks. Add --json for machine-readable output.

Code Means Fix CONFIG_INVALID_VALUE A value has the wrong type or is out of range The message names the file, line and allowed values. CONFIG_SCOPE The setting isn't allowed in this file (a credential destination in a project file, [publish] in a folder, a trust setting in a profile) Move it where the message says. CONFIG_PROFILE_TOOLS [profiles.<name>.tools] Use [toolsets.<name>.tools]. CONFIG_TOOLSET_UNKNOWN --toolset names a toolset this folder doesn't see The message lists the toolsets defined here. CONFIG_TOOLSET_INVALID Bad contexts or platforms, or a non-tool key under a toolset's tools Fix the toolset fields. CONFIG_OVERRIDE_DENIED A value contradicts a policy or project constraint Use an allowed value, or change the constraint. CONFIG_CONSTRAINT_INVALID A [constraints] entry is malformed or names a setting a project can't constrain Follow the message. CONFIG_UNKNOWN_OPTIONAL Unknown section or key (a warning) Check the spelling hint; --strict makes it an error.

CLI reference Published from the canonical docs/reference/plugin-catalog.md file. Features marked experimental remain experimental; check support limitations before relying on them. Every build target in Oyzu is built by a builder plugin. The plugin catalog tells oyzu which plugins exist, how to recognize a project they can build and where to download them. This page explains how oyzu finds the catalog, detects your project, chooses a builder, and shows you what it chose and how to change it. Note: Plugins are experimental. No builder is built into the CLI. Each target needs a plugin from a catalog, a package you bind yourself or a local development binding. When none is available, the build fails with advice; it never falls back to another builder. Today the official catalog lists the Go builder (oyzu/go) as a preview release. See Go builder preview.

Opt in to preview releases in your user configuration (a project file can't set this): [plugins] preview = true Then run oyzu build in a Go module. Oyzu detects go/app from the catalog, downloads oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1 from ghcr.io/oyzuai/plugins/go (anonymously, with its signature checked), records the release in oyzu.lock and builds with it. The build prints the choice in its Selection section with the source official default. You don't need a binding or an account. A plugins.packages binding still works and takes precedence if you want to supply the package yourself.

documents.t: Setting Values Default Where it can be set plugins.preview true, false false User, machine or administrative configuration plugins.packages Table of builder reference to a package archive or OCI release (plugin packages) none User, machine or administrative configuration plugins.development Table of builder reference to a local executable (plugin development) none User, machine or administrative configuration toolIndex.* Which tool index, and so which catalog, to use (tool index) The official index User, machine or administrative configuration These settings select code that runs on your machine, so a project file, oyzu.local.toml or a profile can't set them (CONFIG_SCOPE).

Each command picks one catalog snapshot at the start and keeps it, so two lookups in one command never see different catalogs. The snapshot is the published catalog of your configured tool index: the official one, or your organization's. No catalog is built into the CLI. Tool index plugins.preview Catalog used A real build fetches it Official (default) on The official catalog, plus the preview supplement Yes. A copy fetched in the last 3600 seconds is reused Official off Verified cached copies only. No new preview selection No toolIndex.url = false any None No Organization (toolIndex.identity or toolIndex.trustedRoot set) any Your organization's catalog only Yes. A copy fetched in the last 3600 seconds is reused When a builder in the build came from a catalog, build output names that catalog on the Selection heading, for example official catalog serial 17 or acme catalog serial 3. The serial is the catalog's version number. A build whose builders are all local development executables or direct bindings names no catalog. The Selection section lists only the builders of the builds being built: oyzu build cli doesn't list the docs build's builder. How the catalog is verified. The catalog is plugins.json and plugins.json.sigstore.json, published next to index.json in the tool index release and signed with the same identity (tool index). Oyzu: verifies the signature with the index's trusted root and identity; checks the document's content digest, structure and size limits; refuses a catalog at or after its expires_at; refuses a rollback: a lower serial number, the same serial with different bytes, or a higher serial generated earlier. The last verified copy is kept in <store>/catalogs/plugins/ and the rollback floor in <store>/state/plugins/. If a newly fetched copy is refused, oyzu ignores it and keeps using the last verified copy, including its withdrawals. The 3600-second reuse window is separate from expires_at. A copy can expire sooner and still need a refresh. oyzu build --frozen refreshes catalog metadata the same way, so current withdrawals still apply, but it never changes the locked selection or downloads a missing package. --offline and read-only commands never fetch. Organization catalogs replace the official one. With an organization identity, oyzu never consults the official catalog. If that catalog selects a release and its bytes are unavailable, the build fails. If it has no matching entry, the reference is refused. Another catalog never supplies it.

When no catalog is usable, the reason decides what happens. It's the same for uses: references you write and for detected ones. Why there's no catalog Locked selection Reference not yet locked Refused: a fetched copy failed signature, decoding, expiry or rollback checks and no verified copy is cached, or the cached copy fails those checks Refused on every command, including --plan: PLUGIN_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE Refused: PLUGIN_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE Expired: the last verified copy has expired Replays oyzu.lock against that copy's withdrawals, with the warning PLUGIN_CATALOG_EXPIRED (newer withdrawals may be missing). JSON marks the catalog expired: true Refused Absent: nothing published, reachable or cached, and no catalog was ever verified in this store (a first run offline, or toolIndex.url = false) Replays from oyzu.lock Needs a package or development binding; otherwise PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE A plugins.development or plugins.packages binding for the reference works without a usable catalog, but never past a withdrawal or revocation that the last verified copy (even an expired one) lists for that release. If the network blocks the fetch on a machine that has never verified a catalog, the state is "Absent": a lock replays without any withdrawal check. When a refresh fails and the last verified copy decides, the Selection section shows note using the last verified <catalog>: <reason>, and JSON carries it as catalog.note.

The official catalog lists the Go preview (oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1), its references go/app and go/library, and two detections: go-module (a go.mod with a module line and no go.work) and go-workspace (a go.work). Without plugins.preview, a build reads only the verified cached copy, because there is no stable release to find. With it, a real build refreshes the catalog so withdrawals apply. On a machine that has never obtained the catalog, a builder reference needs a lock entry or a binding.

With the default tool index and plugins.preview on, oyzu can also read a second signed document, plugins-preview.json, from the public plugins-preview release of oyzuai/tool-index. This supplement isn't available yet: no supplement is published, so it adds nothing today. Organization catalogs never fetch it. Once it's published, these rules apply: It can add official preview releases. It can't add stable releases or another publisher's packages, and it can't change or replace anything in the main catalog. Official withdrawals always win. A withdrawal in the supplement matches package, version and root digest together. Each document has its own serial, expiry and rollback state. A preview release found in it is signed by a person's identity (not the release workflow) under Sigstore's production roots. A release marked as a local preview but listed as stable is refused. New downloads need a current verified entry. An expired copy can still refuse a release but can't permit a download. Turning plugins.preview off stops new preview selection; a locked, installed release still replays unless a current refusal applies.

A catalog detection maps files in a directory to a builder reference. The matching is deliberately simple: exact marker file names, a few checks on JSON, TOML and go.mod fields (present, equals, prefix), and all, any and not. There are no globs, paths, expressions or commands. Only detections for references this build could actually use take part: a reference with an eligible release, a lock entry or a binding. Marker names match case-exactly. A symbolic link isn't a marker. A file that can't be parsed counts as having no field, not as an error. The work is bounded: 100,000 directories, 512 parsed files, 32 MiB parsed and 1,024 findings. Reaching a bound fails with PLUGIN_DETECTION_INCOMPLETE; declare your targets in build.yaml to avoid it. An explicit build.yaml is the full list of builds. Detection doesn't run, and an incidental file adds no target. Without one, a directory becomes a target when a catalog detection or a native convention recognizes it. Dependency and output directories are skipped, and nested repositories and build.yaml directories are boundaries. If one directory matches different references (two catalog detections, or a catalog go/app beside a native-convention rust/app), discovery stops with PLUGIN_DETECTION_CONFLICT. It names the evidence for each candidate and the build.yaml line that settles it. If exactly one candidate is already locked, the lock wins and the others become a note.

A reference gets its builder the same way whether you wrote it as uses: in build.yaml, the catalog detected it, or a native convention recognized it. Oyzu tries these in order: A plugins.development binding (plugin development). A plugins.packages binding. If its digest matches the catalog's selected release, it's that release's local archive route, and the package's publisher, name and version are checked against the catalog before installation. Any other digest is a local package binding. A binding for a withdrawn or revoked release is refused with PLUGIN_RELEASE_WITHDRAWN or PLUGIN_RELEASE_REVOKED before it's recorded or launched. A binding that names a different release than oyzu.lock fails with PLUGIN_LOCK_MISMATCH until you remove the lock entry. The release oyzu.lock already holds, replayed even if the catalog now lists a newer one. A locked release that a catalog has withdrawn or revoked is refused, naming the lock entry to remove so the next oyzu build can adopt an eligible release. If an organization catalog now binds the reference to a different package, the build fails with PLUGIN_BINDING_CHANGED so the change is adopted visibly, never silently. The catalog's newest eligible release of the reference's package and profile. A release is not eligible when it is withdrawn or revoked, is a preview and plugins.preview is off, is unsupported, doesn't support protocol generation v1alpha1 or the builder profile, or has no payload for this machine's OS, architecture and ABI. If nothing serves the reference, the build fails with PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE and the catalog's reason. Some packages need a supporting plugin. For example, a Python application container uses the Docker package, and a Docker dependency context uses its own ecosystem's package. Oyzu selects those through the same order and the same organization boundary before it writes the lock or starts any work. If selecting one fails, the lock isn't changed. A frozen or offline build needs the complete locked set.

A real oyzu build downloads a catalog-selected release from an OCI or HTTPS route in its catalog entry, using the same installer as an OCI binding. The download is anonymous, by the listed root digest, with the same package, platform and withdrawal checks. Oyzu records exactly that root in oyzu.lock. When both route types are listed, the first OCI route is used; otherwise the first HTTPS route. A failed route never falls back to another route or catalog. See HTTPS layout archives for the mirror format. With an existing lock and an empty plugin store, an online, non-frozen build downloads the exact locked digest from its entry in the current catalog, even when a newer release is listed. It doesn't rewrite the lock. A release already in the store is reused without a request. Routes only ever come from the verified catalog, never from project files. Only a real oyzu build adopts or installs a plugin. Every other command (build --plan, --check, run, discover) replays the lock and the store. An unadopted catalog selection there fails with PLUGIN_NOT_ADOPTED: nothing is downloaded, installed, launched or written. Help, --version, shell activation and oyzu exec never load a catalog or select a builder.

The signature rule follows the package's publisher, on whatever registry serves it. Package What oyzu requires Publisher oyzu (for example oyzu/go) A signature from the plugin-release.yml workflow of oyzuai/oyzu on refs/heads/main, from a GitHub-hosted runner, verified against Sigstore's production trusted root. This holds for the official ghcr.io/oyzuai/plugins/<name> route and for a company mirror. Nothing in a catalog or in configuration can name another signer or root Any other publisher (for example acme/go on a company registry) Trusted by digest: the signed catalog lists the root digest. No signature is requested A mirror of an official package must therefore serve the release's signature referrers as well as its root, manifests and blobs, and the root it serves must hash to the digest the catalog lists. A refused mirror reports one of: PLUGIN_SIGNATURE_MISSING: no signature referrer. PLUGIN_SIGNATURE_INVALID: no signature verifies for the official signer. PLUGIN_PACKAGE_DIGEST: other bytes under the listed root. Nothing is installed or recorded when a mirror is refused. A company catalog can't pass off its own build as oyzu/go; list it under its own package name instead.
plugins.preview = true makes preview releases eligible. Set it in user, machine or administrative configuration, never in a project file: oyzu config set --global plugins.preview true

A build with plugin-backed targets shows the choice in a Selection section, after Prepare and before Plan. When the build adopted a selection or installed a package, each target gets a full record. Output shortened. -- Selection --- official catalog serial 18 ok go/app project oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1 (adopted) selected by go.mod module (rule go-module, official catalog serial 18) source official default · from official catalog serial 18 · preview release (plugins.preview) package installed now · sha256:0382c192…ee48 · 710.6 KiB · from /home/me/go-0.1.0-preview.1.tar.gz lock recorded in oyzu.lock now; review and commit the diff tool go 1.27.2 · installed now · go.mod requires go >=1.22; nothing pins it not what you wanted? not a go/app target? Declare the targets you want in build.yaml; undeclared directories add none build.yaml: {builds: {project: {uses: <builder>, path: .}}} another implementation of go/app? Bind its package for this reference (or use your organization's catalog) and select again oyzu config set --global --json-value 'plugins.packages."go/app"' '{"archive":"<path>","sha256":"<digest>"}' && rm oyzu.lock undo this adoption: revert oyzu.lock and this reference's settings (plugins.preview is the global preview opt-in) rm oyzu.lock && oyzu config unset --global 'plugins.packages."go/app"' && oyzu config set --global plugins.preview false another go version? Pin it in oyzu.toml oyzu pin go@<version> When nothing changed, each target is one line: -- Selection --- official catalog serial 18 reused go/app project oyzu/go 0.1.0-preview.1 (locked) Field Meaning selected by uses in build.yaml, the catalog detection (evidence, rule and catalog), or the native convention source official default, company binding (organization catalog), local package binding, direct OCI source (an explicit URI), local development binding, or oyzu.lock (a locked release no current source explains). Followed by the catalog that listed it, and preview release (plugins.preview) or prerelease version where it applies package installed now with the release digest, archive size and route, or reused from the store lock Adopted now (a reviewable oyzu.lock diff), replayed, or not locked (development binding) tool Each tool this target needs, its version, whether it was installed now, and why not what you wanted? One copyable fix per case. For an earlier lock, the last line is oyzu plugins update <reference> Notes follow the targets, for example a competing detection kept out by a lock, or why an expired catalog was used. Without color, marks are words (ok, reused). With --json, the same record is in the build manifest under extensions["oyzu.dev/plugin-selection"]. Output shortened. {"catalog":{"label":"official catalog serial 17","source":"fetched","official":true, "serial":17,"expired":false,"note":null}, "catalogChoice":"published","preview":true,"changed":true,"notes":[], "targets":[{"target":"project","path":".","reference":"go/app", "decision":{"kind":"detected","rule":"go-module","evidence":["go.mod module"], "catalog":"official catalog serial 18"}, "source":"official-default","catalog":"official catalog serial 18", "package":"oyzu/go","version":"0.1.0-preview.1","release":"sha256:…", "preview":true,"state":"adopted","installedNow":true, "tools":[{"tool":"go","id":"oyzu:go","requirement":"go.mod requires go >=1.22","pinned":false}], "remedies":[{"case":"undo","summary":"…","action":"…"}]}]} catalogChoice is published, no-index, official-unavailable or organization. oyzu plugins explain prints the same record without adopting, installing or launching anything. There, state can also be not-adopted or not-installed.

Adoption happens only in a real build, always shows up as an oyzu.lock diff, and never prompts. What went wrong Fix A stray file added the wrong ecosystem Declare the targets you want in build.yaml (the printed line). The stray directory adds no target and its builder is never downloaded Right ecosystem, wrong implementation Run the printed oyzu config set --global --json-value 'plugins.packages."<reference>"' … line to bind another package, and remove the lock entry Right builder, wrong tool version oyzu pin <tool>@<version> writes the pin to oyzu.toml Ambiguous evidence (npm and pnpm lockfiles, two catalog detections) Discovery stops and names the smallest build.yaml selector. Nothing is guessed or installed Undo an adoption git checkout -- oyzu.lock (or rm oyzu.lock if this build created it), then remove the reference's plugins.packages entry if it supplied the bytes, and turn plugins.preview off for a catalog preview

Code Cause Recovery PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE No plugin serves the reference. The message gives the catalog's reason, for example "preview only" Turn on plugins.preview, or bind a package PLUGIN_DETECTION_CONFLICT Different references match one directory Declare the target with uses: in build.yaml PLUGIN_DETECTION_INCOMPLETE A detection work bound was reached Declare the targets in build.yaml PLUGIN_RELEASE_WITHDRAWN, PLUGIN_RELEASE_REVOKED A catalog (an expired copy included) withdrew or revoked the locked release, or the release a plugins.packages binding names Run oyzu plugins update <reference> (it needs a binding or the store to supply the replacement), or remove the named [[plugin]] entry and build. For a binding, bind an eligible release or run the oyzu config unset --global … line the error prints. oyzu plugins list marks refused copies (withdrawn) or (revoked) and nothing can select them PLUGIN_BINDING_CHANGED The organization catalog binds the reference to a different package than the lock Remove the named [[plugin]] entry and build to adopt the new binding PLUGIN_LOCK_MISMATCH A plugins.packages binding names a different release than the lock Remove the lock entry, or restore the binding PLUGIN_LOCK_MISSING build --frozen needs a plugin selection that's not in the lock Restore the complete lock PLUGIN_LOCK_UNUSABLE A locked release is missing and --frozen or --offline forbids downloading it, or no current catalog entry supplies it Run an online, non-frozen oyzu build that can reach the route PLUGIN_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE A new catalog selection has no usable download route, or this run forbids it Run online, or bind the archive with the release digest (plugins.packages) PLUGIN_ROUTE_FAILED The release's route can't be used (registry unreachable, release missing, or an unusable address). Nothing was installed or recorded Restore access to the route. Signature, digest and package failures have their own codes PLUGIN_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE No usable catalog and the catalog was refused, or an unlocked reference met an expired one Restore access to the catalog, or use a binding. Oyzu never falls back to another catalog PLUGIN_CATALOG_EXPIRED (warning) A lock replayed against an expired catalog's withdrawals Run an online oyzu build to refresh. If the refresh was refused, fix the catalog source PLUGIN_PACKAGE_MISMATCH The archive isn't the catalog's package and version Bind the right archive PLUGIN_NOT_ADOPTED A command other than oyzu build met an unadopted selection Run oyzu build

--frozen and --offline never download from a catalog route. A missing locked release needs an online build or a binding. Without plugins.preview, builds don't refresh the official catalog. The inspection commands have an explicit --refresh, which doesn't grant preview selection. A catalog entry lists the platforms a release was built for (macOS, Linux and Windows). Go builds through an HTTPS mirror have been tested on Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64. Other platforms in a package aren't tested. A revocation refuses selection and launch of an installed release, even from an expired copy. The bytes stay in the store until you run oyzu plugins prune SHA256... --apply. @vN major selectors in uses aren't supported. Update with oyzu plugins update. oyzu config validate only replays what's already locked. It never adopts a release or installs a package.
